# Signature beats

A signature beat is the one moment a player remembers. Every effect picks
ONE or TWO (more and nothing stands out). Counts are from the corpus batches
(of ~10 per batch); "family" says where it belongs. Each has a Roblox build.

| Beat | Seen | Family | Build in Roblox |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Dark beat before release** (black/grey frames, lights dim, charge collapses) | 6/10 beams, 6/10 impacts, 6/10 auras | all (anime strongest) | ColorCorrection Brightness -0.4..-0.8 for 2-20 frames, or dim the charge emitters to 0 just before the flash |
| **Suck-in / contraction** before a burst | 4/14 moves, cone contracts 4 frames | anime, game | tween the charge mesh/ring Size down 15-30 % in 0.06-0.1 s (Quart In), then release |
| **1-2 frame white flash, hard off** | most strikes, teleports, reactions | anime, game (contact only) | ColorCorrection Brightness 1 for 1 frame or a white ScreenGui Frame |
| **Held, tinted whiteout** then a cooling arc | climaxes (8/10 auras tinted) | anime set-pieces | ColorCorrection Brightness 0.9 + TintColor, hold 0.3-1.6 s, then tween TintColor through cream/yellow/orange (or the theme's arc) |
| **Inverted / B&W impact frames**, black separators, stepped on 3s | 5/10 beams, 5/10 impacts, 4/4 ultimates | anime big moves only | full-screen ScreenGui images or Saturation -1 + Contrast frames; 8-17 frames total |
| **Escalating impact frames** (each bigger) | 5/10 impacts | anime | 2-3 impact frame groups, each with a larger burst sprite |
| **Colour swap at release / through white** | 5/13 elemental, KonoSuba, Super Saiyan | anime, game reactions | charge in hue A; flash; everything after in hue B (complementary) |
| **Cut to a far wide shot** for the payoff | 5/10 beams, set-pieces | anime, realistic | CameraType Scriptable, cut (no tween) to a wide locked-off CFrame; restore after |
| **World regrade per phase** (desaturate on charge, sky darkens first) | 7/10 auras, 6/10 impacts | anime, realistic | ColorCorrection Saturation -0.6 + TintColor, Lighting/Atmosphere tweens |
| **Shape born at full size** (no grow-in) | slashes, 6/10 impacts | all | emit the crescent/burst at final Size on frame 1, animate rotation/fade not scale |
| **Squash to a dome + horizontal shock ring** | explosions | anime | sphere shells tween to 1.2:0.62:1.2 while a flat ring mesh races to 5R |
| **Strobe / flicker in sustain** (1-2 frames per state) | 6/10 beams | anime beams | toggle core Transparency or swap texture every 2 frames; keep < 3 Hz for full-screen strobes |
| **Helical rings / segments** on a beam | SBC, Godzilla vs Kong | anime, realistic | spiral mesh or Beam pairs with CurveSize, rings spawned along the path |
| **Stacked staggered circles** | KonoSuba, Roblox showcases | anime | plane meshes with SurfaceAppearance sigils, scale in 0.4 s Quart Out, 0.1-0.25 s apart |
| **Telegraph line** before damage | game beams (2/2) | stylised_game | thin Beam along the path, colour yellow -> orange -> red over ~0.9 s |
| **Residue that outlasts the hit** (scorch, ice, smoke, embers, hanging glyph) | 6-7 per batch | all | decal/plane mesh, slow-fading particles, physics rock Parts |
| **Opposing elements make a third state** | 3/13 | game, anime | two coloured charges meet; the burst uses a THIRD hue (steam, purple, shower) |
| **Payoff held still** (freeze frame) | 3/10 auras | anime | TimeScale 0 on emitters + pause tweens for 0.2-0.5 s, then resume |
| **Streaks wrap the target, reappear in end pose** | Raijin | anime dash | Trails/Beams spiral round the target for 0.2 s, character teleported between white frames |
| **Two-stage onset** (pop to ~35 %, hold, surge) | Godzilla Minus One | realistic, anime | width tween to 0.35 (Quart Out 0.05 s), hold 0.4 s, then surge to 1.0 (Quad In) |

# Designing an ORIGINAL effect with no reference

Why this exists (2026-10-26): the KonoSuba-referenced explosion looked good;
the no-reference slash "doesnt look amazing". The reference supplied five
things the slash lacked: a timeline, motion curves, a colour story, a
signature beat, and staging. Without a reference they come from here:
the brief (intent), `references/corpus/` (measured skeletons),
`references/styles/` (look family), `references/BEATS.md` (the memorable
moment). Do every step; skipping the brief is exactly how the slash failed.

## 1. Write the brief (in the builder file's docstring)

```
Name:            <move name>
Fantasy:         <one line: what the player feels>
Tier:            basic | skill | big skill | ultimate   (sets the time budget, STYLES.md)
Style family:    anime_cel | realistic | stylised_game
Category:        beam | slash | impact | explosion | orb_charge | aura_transform | projectile | dash_teleport | elemental | ambient_pickup | ultimate
Shape word:      ONE word (crescent, shatter, bloom, spiral, needle, petal, fracture...)
Dominant hue:    #hex           Accent: #hex (complementary or cool vs warm)   Darks: #hex
Colour arc:      e.g. violet charge -> white flash -> gold body -> ash residue
Signature beat:  1-2 from BEATS.md (+ one twist of our own)
Timeline:        phases with seconds, taken from the category skeleton below, scaled to the tier
Staging:         camera (gameplay / cut / wide), shake, world grade
Residue:         what stays, and for how long (residue:main ratio)
```

Uniqueness comes from the shape word, the palette, and the twist on the
signature beat. Quality comes from the skeleton and the style rules.

## 2. Get the skeleton from the corpus

`python scripts/corpus_stats.py --cat <category>` prints the measured phase
shares, anticipation:release and residue:main ranges, flash frequency and
frames, layer counts and roles. Use the median as the target and stay inside
p25..p75 unless the brief says why not. `references/corpus/CATEGORIES.md`
holds the condensed skeleton per category.

## 3. Assets
Textures from `sim/tex/make_textures.py` (study-measured recipes; add a new
category there, then `texture-study/measure.py` against the references);
meshes from `sim/mesh/make_meshes.py`. Match the STYLE FAMILY: cel textures
for anime_cel, soft/blended for realistic, bright clean sprites for game.

## 4. Build as a parametric builder
`sim/effects/build_<name>.py`, every number from the brief + skeleton,
scaled from one size parameter. Layer roles to cover (corpus median 6-9
layers): flash, core, body, secondary strokes, sparks, ground, residue,
screen, light. Distinct lifetimes per layer.

## 5. Critic loop (do not grade your own work by eye alone)
1. **Numeric gate:** `python scripts/critic_gate.py sim/effects/<file>.json
   [--metrics strip_metrics.json]` checks the definition against the category
   skeleton and the universal rules (flash hard-off, peak in the first quarter
   of the main event, residue ratio in range, layer count, distinct
   lifetimes, accent present, no linear whole-effect fades, strobe < 3 Hz).
   Fix every FAIL.
2. **Blind review:** spawn ONE reviewer agent with: a numbered strip of our
   effect and 2-3 strips of pro corpus effects of the same category (from
   `<your VFX research folder>/corpus/<batch>/sheets`, set in `LOCAL.md`), shuffled and
   unlabelled, plus `references/styles/<family>.md`. Ask: "rank these by
   professional quality; for the weakest, list the 3 concrete defects in
   VFX terms". If ours ranks last, fix the named defects and repeat (max 3
   rounds; then report honestly).
3. Render the MP4 (`app.captureFrame(t, 1920, 1080)` per frame, POST each
   to `/save`, ffmpeg at 60 fps) for the user.

Blind strips: `app.strip(times, {blind: true})` labels frames `#n` only.
Without it the luma readout identified our strips to the reviewer.

## What the first blind reviews taught (2026-10-27, Eclipse Rend + Riptide Lance)

Scores out of 10 against pro strips: Eclipse Rend climbed from "last,
procedural" to 6/10 over four rounds (a pro Roblox slash scored 5, the Twist
VFX slash 7.5); Riptide Lance 4.5. The defects that kept recurring are now
rules:

1. **Geometric regularity is the giveaway.** Exact circles, evenly spaced
   spikes or rings, ruler-straight lines, identical repeated sprites, flat
   slab fills: "a parameter preset, not a drawing". Use the PAINTED tier
   (`sim/tex/vfxpaint.py` brush engine, `sim/tex/make_painted.py`): every
   shape is many tapered, wandering strokes of different weight and value.
2. **Never a full-screen white for a skill.** The flash is local (flare at
   the contact) or thematic (an eclipse DARKENS); full white only for
   ultimates, 1-2 frames.
3. **Dark layers must be translucent and fade at the edges,** or they read
   as an opaque black slab.
4. **A white-hot leading edge along the whole stroke** that cools to the
   hue: a separate rim layer painted from the SAME strokes (qmax filter),
   thin, not a second body.
5. **Erode over 6-8 frames, don't fade;** keep residue ~0.4 s for a skill
   and attach it to the effect.
6. **Additive cores eat the body colour:** keep the core thin and the body
   alpha-blended (LightEmission ~0.35) or the beam reads pure white.
7. **Check every CFrame "by" spec:** [x,y,z,rx,ry,rz], a rotation in the
   translation slots flew rings 120 studs away.
Open: the reviewer still wants the crescent to draw on over 2-3 frames and
sweep (it holds), the beam to lose its uniform cylinder look, and impact
sparks in the beam's palette.

# ParticleEmitter property surface

**Measured 2026-08-26** by probing a live emitter in Studio with `pcall` reads,
not copied from documentation. 33 candidates tested, 33 exist, 0 missing.

The reason this file exists: the Studio MCP's `get_class_info` and
`get_instance_properties` both report only nine fields for a ParticleEmitter
(`Name`, `ClassName`, `Parent`, `Size`, `Rotation`, `Transparency`, `Color`,
`Enabled`, `Brightness`). That is **6 of 31 real properties**. Anything harvested
through them is silently three quarters empty.

## Measured defaults on a fresh emitter

| Property | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Texture` | `rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds` | one of only three stock textures that exist |
| `Rate` | `20` | per second, continuous |
| `Speed` | `5, 5` | NumberRange, studs/s |
| `Lifetime` | `5, 10` | NumberRange, seconds. Far too long for most effects |
| `Shape` | `Box` | Sphere / Cylinder / Disc also valid |
| `EmissionDirection` | `Top` | NormalId |
| `Orientation` | `FacingCamera` | also `VelocityParallel`, `VelocityPerpendicular` |
| `ZOffset` | `0` | pushes toward (+) or away from (-) the camera |
| `Squash` | `0..0` | NumberSequence |

## Full list, by type

**number**: `Brightness`, `Drag`, `LightEmission`, `LightInfluence`, `Rate`,
`TimeScale`, `VelocityInheritance`, `ZOffset`

**boolean**: `Enabled`, `FlipbookStartRandom`, `LockedToPart`, `WindAffectsDrag`

**string**: `Texture`

**Vector3**: `Acceleration`

**Vector2**: `SpreadAngle`

**NumberRange**: `FlipbookFramerate`, `Lifetime`, `RotSpeed`, `Rotation`, `Speed`

**NumberSequence**: `Size`, `Squash`, `Transparency`

**ColorSequence**: `Color`

**EnumItem**: `EmissionDirection` (NormalId), `FlipbookLayout`
(ParticleFlipbookLayout), `FlipbookMode` (ParticleFlipbookMode), `Orientation`
(ParticleOrientation), `Shape` (ParticleEmitterShape), `ShapeInOut`
(ParticleEmitterShapeInOut), `ShapeStyle` (ParticleEmitterShapeStyle)

`LocalTransparencyModifier` also reads but is a client-side render override, not
part of the effect definition, so it is excluded from harvesting.

## Emission volume

There is **no emitter-size property**. `Shape` selects the volume's form and
`ShapeStyle` selects Volume (fill) or Surface (shell), but the volume itself is
approximately unit-sized when the emitter sits under an Attachment. Parent to a
larger BasePart to grow it.

Practical consequence on a character: every particle spawns inside the torso and
is occluded. Cover a body by making particles large enough to overlap the
silhouette, or fast enough to escape it.

## Beam and Trail

`Attachment0` and `Attachment1` are **instance references, not values**. They
cannot be serialised as data and are recorded as `{"Ref": "<full name>"}`. They
are structure to be rebuilt on the target rig, never faked.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Recipe JSON -> a self-contained Luau ModuleScript.

The recipes are the single source of truth. This emitter and the live Studio
builder read the SAME files, so what you tuned in Studio and what ships cannot
disagree about a value.
"""
import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys

def default_lib() -> pathlib.Path:
    """Your own recipe folder: --lib, or the ROBLOX_VFX_LIB env var (see LOCAL.md).

    No effects ship with this skill, so there is no built-in library to fall back
    to. If the library folder has a recipes/ subfolder, that is what is used."""
    v = os.environ.get("ROBLOX_VFX_LIB")
    if not v and (pathlib.Path.home() / "Roblox-VFX-Library").is_dir():
        v = str(pathlib.Path.home() / "Roblox-VFX-Library")  # the setup skill's default
    if not v:
        raise SystemExit("no recipe library given: pass --lib <your VFX library folder> "
                         "or set ROBLOX_VFX_LIB (the path is in LOCAL.md)")
    p = pathlib.Path(v).expanduser()
    return p / "recipes" if (p / "recipes").is_dir() else p


COMPACT = False  # set by --compact: one line per table, same data


def lua(v, ind=0):
    p = "\t" * ind
    if COMPACT and isinstance(v, dict):
        return "{" + ", ".join(
            "%s = %s" % (k if k.isidentifier() else '["%s"]' % k, lua(val)) for k, val in v.items()) + "}"
    if isinstance(v, bool):
        return "true" if v else "false"
    if isinstance(v, float):
        return repr(round(v, 6))
    if isinstance(v, int):
        return str(v)
    if isinstance(v, str):
        return '"' + v.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"') + '"'
    if isinstance(v, list):
        return "{" + ", ".join(lua(x, ind) for x in v) + "}"
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        parts = []
        for k, val in v.items():
            key = k if k.isidentifier() else '["%s"]' % k
            parts.append("%s\t%s = %s" % (p, key, lua(val, ind + 1)))
        return "{\n" + ",\n".join(parts) + "\n" + p + "}"
    if v is None:
        return "nil"
    raise TypeError(type(v))


HEAD = r'''--# selene: allow(multiple_statements, shadowing, unused_variable)
-- GENERATED by roblox-vfx/scripts/emit_luau.py. Do not hand-edit.
-- (The selene line above: a generated file is linted as generated. A real
-- project's selene gate failed on this file's one-line ifs.)
-- Edit the recipe JSON and regenerate, or tune live in Studio and harvest back.
local VFXKit = {}

local function dec(v)
	if type(v) ~= "table" then return v end
	if v.Enum then
		local cls, item = string.match(v.Enum, "^([%w_]+)%.([%w_]+)$")
		return Enum[cls][item]
	elseif v.Vector3 then return Vector3.new(v.Vector3[1], v.Vector3[2], v.Vector3[3])
	elseif v.Vector2 then return Vector2.new(v.Vector2[1], v.Vector2[2])
	elseif v.Color3 then return Color3.new(v.Color3[1], v.Color3[2], v.Color3[3])
	elseif v.NumberRange then return NumberRange.new(v.NumberRange[1], v.NumberRange[2])
	elseif v.NumberSequence then
		local kp = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(v.NumberSequence) do
			table.insert(kp, NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(k[1], k[2], k[3] or 0))
		end
		return NumberSequence.new(kp)
	elseif v.ColorSequence then
		local kp = {}
		for _, k in ipairs(v.ColorSequence) do
			table.insert(kp, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(k[1], Color3.new(k[2][1], k[2][2], k[2][3])))
		end
		return ColorSequence.new(kp)
	end
	return nil
end

local function scaleSeq(seq, k)
	local kp = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(seq.Keypoints) do
		table.insert(kp, NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(p.Time, p.Value * k, p.Envelope * k))
	end
	return NumberSequence.new(kp)
end

-- Tint keeps the LUMINANCE ramp and replaces only the hue. A flat colour swap
-- destroys the bright-core-to-dark-tail arc, which is the thing that reads as fire.
local function tintSeq(seq, c)
	local kp = {}
	for _, p in ipairs(seq.Keypoints) do
		local lum = 0.2126 * p.Value.R + 0.7152 * p.Value.G + 0.0722 * p.Value.B
		table.insert(kp, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(p.Time, Color3.new(
			math.clamp(c.R * lum * 1.6, 0, 1),
			math.clamp(c.G * lum * 1.6, 0, 1),
			math.clamp(c.B * lum * 1.6, 0, 1))))
	end
	return ColorSequence.new(kp)
end

--[[
	VFXKit.build(recipeName, targetPart, opts) -> handle

	targetPart MUST be a BasePart. An Attachment parented to a Model or a Folder
	has no world position, so the effect builds silently at the world origin and
	looks like it simply did not fire.

	opts = { scale, tint (Color3), lifetime_mul, rate_mul, offset (Vector3), suffix }
	handle = { emit(mult), setEnabled(bool), destroy() }
]]
function VFXKit.build(name, target, opts)
	opts = opts or {}
	local recipe = VFXKit.Recipes[name]
	assert(recipe, "roblox-vfx: no recipe named " .. tostring(name))
	assert(typeof(target) == "Instance" and target:IsA("BasePart"),
		"roblox-vfx: build target must be a BasePart, got "
		.. tostring(target and target.ClassName))

	local scale = opts.scale or 1
	local tag = name .. (opts.suffix or "")
	local base = opts.offset or Vector3.new(0, 0, 0)

	for _, c in ipairs(target:GetChildren()) do
		if c:IsA("Attachment") and c:GetAttribute("VFXTag") == tag then c:Destroy() end
	end

	local emitters, lights, ribbons = {}, {}, {}
	for _, layer in ipairs(recipe.layers) do
		local att = Instance.new("Attachment")
		att.Name = tag .. "_" .. layer.name
		att:SetAttribute("VFXTag", tag)
		att.Position = base + Vector3.new(
			layer.offset[1] * scale, layer.offset[2] * scale, layer.offset[3] * scale)
		att.Parent = target

		local inst = Instance.new(layer.class)
		inst.Name = layer.name
		for k, v in pairs(layer.props) do
			local d = dec(v)
			if d ~= nil then pcall(function() inst[k] = d end) end
		end

		if scale ~= 1 then
			pcall(function() inst.Size = scaleSeq(inst.Size, scale) end)
			pcall(function() inst.Speed = NumberRange.new(inst.Speed.Min * scale, inst.Speed.Max * scale) end)
			pcall(function() inst.Acceleration = inst.Acceleration * scale end)
			pcall(function() inst.Range = inst.Range * scale end)
		end
		if opts.tint then pcall(function() inst.Color = tintSeq(inst.Color, opts.tint) end) end
		if opts.lifetime_mul then
			pcall(function()
				inst.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(
					inst.Lifetime.Min * opts.lifetime_mul, inst.Lifetime.Max * opts.lifetime_mul)
			end)
		end
		if opts.rate_mul then pcall(function() inst.Rate = inst.Rate * opts.rate_mul end) end

		local em = layer.emit or {}
		inst:SetAttribute("EmitMode", em.mode or "continuous")
		inst:SetAttribute("VFXTag", tag)
		if em.count then inst:SetAttribute("EmitCount", math.max(1, math.floor(em.count * scale))) end
		if em.seconds then inst:SetAttribute("PulseSeconds", em.seconds) end
		if em.from then inst:SetAttribute("PulseFrom", em.from * scale) end

		-- A burst layer must never also stream, or the effect never stops.
		if em.mode == "burst" then pcall(function() inst.Rate = 0 end) end
		if inst:IsA("PointLight") and em.mode == "pulse" then inst.Brightness = 0 end

		-- A Beam/Trail is STRUCTURE, not values: without both attachments wired it
		-- builds fine, passes every check, and draws absolutely nothing.
		if (inst:IsA("Trail") or inst:IsA("Beam")) and layer.endpoints then
			local eps = {}
			for i, e in ipairs(layer.endpoints) do
				local ea = Instance.new("Attachment")
				ea.Name = tag .. "_" .. layer.name .. "_A" .. i
				ea:SetAttribute("VFXTag", tag)
				ea.Position = base + Vector3.new(
					e.offset[1] * scale, e.offset[2] * scale, e.offset[3] * scale)
				ea.Parent = target
				eps[i] = ea
			end
			inst.Attachment0, inst.Attachment1 = eps[1], eps[2]
		end

		inst.Parent = att
		if inst:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then
			table.insert(emitters, inst)
		elseif inst:IsA("PointLight") then
			table.insert(lights, inst)
		elseif inst:IsA("Trail") or inst:IsA("Beam") then
			table.insert(ribbons, inst)
		end
	end

	local handle = {}

	function handle.emit(mult)
		mult = mult or 1
		for _, e in ipairs(emitters) do
			if e:GetAttribute("EmitMode") == "burst" then
				e:Emit(math.max(1, math.floor((e:GetAttribute("EmitCount") or 1) * mult)))
			end
		end
		for _, l in ipairs(lights) do
			if l:GetAttribute("EmitMode") == "pulse" then
				local peak = (l:GetAttribute("PulseFrom") or 6) * mult
				local secs = l:GetAttribute("PulseSeconds") or 0.25
				l.Brightness = peak
				task.spawn(function()
					local t0 = os.clock()
					while l.Parent do
						local a = (os.clock() - t0) / secs
						if a >= 1 then break end
						l.Brightness = peak * (1 - a) * (1 - a)
						task.wait()
					end
					if l.Parent then l.Brightness = 0 end
				end)
			end
		end
	end

	function handle.setEnabled(on)
		for _, e in ipairs(emitters) do
			if e:GetAttribute("EmitMode") == "continuous" then e.Enabled = on end
		end
		for _, l in ipairs(lights) do
			if l:GetAttribute("EmitMode") == "constant" then l.Enabled = on end
		end
		for _, r in ipairs(ribbons) do
			if r:GetAttribute("EmitMode") ~= "burst" then r.Enabled = on end
		end
	end

	function handle.destroy()
		for _, c in ipairs(target:GetChildren()) do
			if c:IsA("Attachment") and c:GetAttribute("VFXTag") == tag then c:Destroy() end
		end
	end

	handle.emitters, handle.lights, handle.ribbons, handle.tag = emitters, lights, ribbons, tag
	return handle
end

'''


def main():
    import argparse
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    # Your library lives outside the skill folder. --lib or ROBLOX_VFX_LIB.
    ap.add_argument("--lib", default=None, help="recipe dir (default: $ROBLOX_VFX_LIB)")
    ap.add_argument("out", nargs="?", default=None, help="output .lua path")
    # 2026-10-08 (a creature game): 45 effects inlined blew past Roblox's 200,000-char
    # Source cap (trap 19) - a file that size installs as NOTHING ("Unable to assign
    # property Source") while every offline gate stays green. --compact writes each
    # table on one line (identical data, ~half the size); the guard refuses to write
    # an oversize module unless --allow-oversize.
    ap.add_argument("--compact", action="store_true", help="one line per table (exclude the file from stylua)")
    ap.add_argument("--nocheck", action="store_true", help="prepend --!nocheck (project .luaurc is strict)")
    ap.add_argument("--allow-oversize", action="store_true")
    # 2026-10-09 (a 143-recipe roster ~ 560K chars): one module cannot
    # hold them (trap 19). --data-dir NAME writes the recipe data as chunk modules
    # in a SIBLING folder <out dir>/NAME/Recipes<k>.luau, each under --chunk-chars,
    # and the main module merges them into VFXKit.Recipes at require time. Sibling,
    # not an init.luau folder module: Lune 0.8 resolves "./x" from init.luau against
    # the PARENT directory, so a folder module loads in Studio and breaks offline checks.
    ap.add_argument("--data-dir", default=None, help="split recipe data into sibling chunk modules")
    ap.add_argument("--chunk-chars", type=int, default=180000)
    a = ap.parse_args()
    global COMPACT
    COMPACT = a.compact
    lib = pathlib.Path(a.lib).resolve() if a.lib else default_lib()

    recipes = {}
    for p in sorted(lib.glob("*.json")):
        d = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        recipes[d["name"]] = {
            "name": d["name"],
            "duration": d.get("duration", 2),
            "texture_portable": d.get("texture_portable", False),
            "layers": [
                {
                    "name": L["name"],
                    "class": L["class"],
                    "offset": L["offset"],
                    "emit": {k: v for k, v in (L.get("emit") or {}).items() if v is not None},
                    "props": L["props"],
                    # Beam/Trail endpoints are structure. Dropping them here was
                    # a silent way to ship a ribbon that draws nothing.
                    **({"endpoints": L["endpoints"]} if L.get("endpoints") else {}),
                }
                for L in d["layers"]
            ],
        }
    if a.data_dir:
        return emit_split(a, recipes)
    body = HEAD + "VFXKit.Recipes = " + lua(recipes) + "\n\nreturn VFXKit\n"
    if a.nocheck:
        body = "--!nocheck\n" + body
    if len(body) >= 200000 and not a.allow_oversize:
        print("FAIL %d chars >= 200000: Roblox will refuse this Source (trap 19). "
              "Use --compact, curate fewer layers, or split." % len(body))
        sys.exit(1)
    out = pathlib.Path(a.out) if a.out else pathlib.Path("references/VFXKit.lua")
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8")
    print("%s %d chars, recipes: %s" % (out, len(body), ", ".join(recipes)))


CHUNK_HEAD = ("--!nocheck\n--# selene: allow(multiple_statements, shadowing, unused_variable)\n"
              "-- GENERATED by roblox-vfx/scripts/emit_luau.py --data-dir. Do not hand-edit.\n"
              "-- Recipe data chunk %d of %d for VFXKit (split under Roblox's 200,000-char Source cap).\n")


def emit_split(a, recipes):
    out = pathlib.Path(a.out)
    ddir = out.parent / a.data_dir
    chunks, cur, size = [], {}, 0
    for name, r in recipes.items():
        n = len(lua({name: r}))
        if cur and size + n > a.chunk_chars:
            chunks.append(cur)
            cur, size = {}, 0
        cur[name] = r
        size += n
    if cur:
        chunks.append(cur)
    ddir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    for old in ddir.glob("Recipes*.luau"):
        old.unlink()
    for k, c in enumerate(chunks, 1):
        body = CHUNK_HEAD % (k, len(chunks)) + "return " + lua(c) + "\n"
        if len(body) >= 200000:
            print("FAIL chunk %d is %d chars >= 200000" % (k, len(body)))
            sys.exit(1)
        (ddir / ("Recipes%d.luau" % k)).write_text(body, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    loader = (
        "VFXKit.Recipes = {}\n"
        "-- data chunks live in the sibling folder %s (Roblox: script.Parent.%s; Lune: a relative path)\n"
        "for k = 1, %d do\n"
        "\tlocal chunk\n"
        "\tif script ~= nil then\n"
        "\t\tchunk = require(script.Parent:WaitForChild(\"%s\"):WaitForChild(\"Recipes\" .. k))\n"
        "\telse\n"
        "\t\t-- selene: allow(incorrect_standard_library_use)\n"
        "\t\tchunk = require(\"./%s/Recipes\" .. k)\n"
        "\tend\n"
        "\tfor name, r in pairs(chunk) do\n"
        "\t\tVFXKit.Recipes[name] = r\n"
        "\tend\n"
        "end\n"
    ) % (a.data_dir, a.data_dir, len(chunks), a.data_dir, a.data_dir)
    body = HEAD + loader + "\nreturn VFXKit\n"
    if a.nocheck:
        body = "--!nocheck\n" + body
    out.write_text(body, encoding="utf-8", newline="\n")
    sizes = ", ".join(str((ddir / ("Recipes%d.luau" % k)).stat().st_size) for k in range(1, len(chunks) + 1))
    print("%s %d chars + %d chunk(s) in %s (%s chars), %d recipes" % (out, len(body), len(chunks), ddir, sizes, len(recipes)))
