-- ENGINE. The element + timeline machine, shared by BOTH front ends:
--
--   scene.lua    edit mode - a stage of anchor Parts, a freeze time, a camera
--   runtime.lua  play mode - the live player character, no freeze, cleanup
--
-- It lives in one file ON PURPOSE. The whole premise of this skill is that what
-- you tuned and what ships cannot disagree; two copies of a 400-line engine is
-- exactly how they start to.
--
-- Everything animates off ONE hand-written stepper rather than TweenService, so
-- a scene can be frozen mid-flight at an exact time and photographed. A
-- TweenService tween cannot be frozen, only cancelled, and cancelling loses the
-- pose - which would make phase-frozen capture impossible for anything but the
-- particles.
--
-- Expects VFX (the codec) already in scope. ctx supplies everything that is
-- NOT the same between the two front ends:
--   ctx.anchorPos(a)      name or {x,y,z} -> Vector3
--   ctx.folder            Instance to build into
--   ctx.sourceModel(n)    Model for clone/model elements
--   ctx.report(str)       progress sink
--   ctx.onFinish(freeze)  optional, called once playback ends
--   ctx.offset(o)         optional, composition offset {x,y,z} -> world Vector3
--   ctx.basis             optional, CFrame rotation applied to every part
--
-- OFFSETS ARE IN COMPOSITION SPACE, NOT WORLD SPACE. Fixed 2026-09-10. Before
-- this, every positional offset went through a plain Vector3.new, which is
-- correct in the edit stage (the stage rig faces -Z, so composition space and
-- world space coincide) and WRONG IN GAME, where a player can face anywhere:
-- "three studs in front of the caster" landed three studs toward world -Z
-- whatever the caster was looking at. It never showed because the first
-- effects only ever offset vertically. The runtime now supplies ctx.offset to
-- map x right / y up / -z forward through the character's own frame, and
-- ctx.basis so a wall or a beam turns WITH the caster instead of staying locked
-- to the world grid. Edit mode passes neither and behaves exactly as before.
local function makeEngine(comp, ctx)
	local anchorPos = ctx.anchorPos
	local fx = ctx.folder
	local ws = workspace

	local function vec(o) o = o or {0, 0, 0}; return Vector3.new(o[1], o[2], o[3]) end
	-- POSITIONAL offsets only. Sizes, accelerations and a layer's attachment
	-- offset on its own host part stay plain vectors via vec().
	local off = ctx.offset or vec
	local basis = ctx.basis or CFrame.new()
	local function c3(t, d) if not t then return d end return Color3.new(t[1], t[2], t[3]) end
	local function mat(n) return n and Enum.Material[n] or Enum.Material.Neon end

	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- easing
	local E = {}
	E.linear  = function(a) return a end
	E.quadOut = function(a) return 1 - (1 - a) ^ 2 end
	E.quadIn  = function(a) return a * a end
	E.cubeOut = function(a) return 1 - (1 - a) ^ 3 end
	E.cubeIn  = function(a) return a * a * a end
	E.expoOut = function(a) return a >= 1 and 1 or 1 - 2 ^ (-10 * a) end
	E.backOut = function(a) local c = 1.70158; return 1 + (c + 1) * (a - 1) ^ 3 + c * (a - 1) ^ 2 end
	E.pulse   = function(a) return math.sin(a * math.pi) end
	local function ease(n) return E[n or "linear"] or E.linear end

	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- elements
	local EL = {}
	local ALL_EMITTERS = {}
	local INITIAL = {}      -- closures restoring each element's authored look

	local function newPart(name, parent)
		local p = Instance.new("Part")
		p.Name = name; p.Anchored = true; p.CanCollide = false; p.CanQuery = false
		p.CanTouch = false; p.CastShadow = false
		p.TopSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth; p.BottomSurface = Enum.SurfaceType.Smooth
		p.Parent = parent
		return p
	end

	-- Tint keeps the LUMINANCE ramp and swaps hue. A flat colour replacement
	-- destroys the bright-core-to-dark-tail arc that is the thing reading as fire.
	local function tintSeq(seq, rgb)
		local kp = {}
		for _, p in ipairs(seq.Keypoints) do
			local lum = 0.2126 * p.Value.R + 0.7152 * p.Value.G + 0.0722 * p.Value.B
			table.insert(kp, ColorSequenceKeypoint.new(p.Time, Color3.new(
				math.clamp(rgb[1] * lum * 1.6, 0, 1),
				math.clamp(rgb[2] * lum * 1.6, 0, 1),
				math.clamp(rgb[3] * lum * 1.6, 0, 1))))
		end
		return ColorSequence.new(kp)
	end
	local function scaleSeq(seq, k)
		local kp = {}
		for _, p in ipairs(seq.Keypoints) do
			table.insert(kp, NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(p.Time, p.Value * k, p.Envelope * k))
		end
		return NumberSequence.new(kp)
	end

	-- Build particle layers out of an inlined recipe.
	-- LAYER SUBSETTING IS NOT OPTIONAL. Plenty of "multi-layer" harvested recipes
	-- are VARIANT SHEETS, not layered effects: Lightning_2 ships ToonLightning,
	-- ToonLightningContrast, ToonLightningDupe and PixelLightning, which are four
	-- art styles of ONE bolt meant to be used one at a time. Build all four and you
	-- get four styles stacked on each other.
	local function buildRecipe(e, host)
		local rec = comp.recipes[e.recipe]
		if not rec then error("SCENE_ERROR recipe not inlined: " .. tostring(e.recipe)) end
		-- Selection is BY NAME, with "#n" for by-index. They must not share a
		-- namespace: pack layers are routinely NAMED "1".."9" (Hit1 is), so a plain
		-- "3" matching both the third layer and every layer called "3" quietly
		-- selects more than was asked for - measured, 7 layers built for a list of 5.
		local wantName, wantIdx = nil, nil
		if e.layers then
			wantName, wantIdx = {}, {}
			for _, v in ipairs(e.layers) do
				local s = tostring(v)
				local n = string.match(s, "^#(%d+)$")
				if n then wantIdx[tonumber(n)] = true else wantName[s] = true end
			end
		end
		local scale = e.scale or 1
		local emitters = {}
		local total = 0
		local skipped = 0
		for i, layer in ipairs(rec.layers) do
			total = total + 1
			local keep = true
			if wantName then keep = (wantIdx[i] or wantName[layer.name]) and true or false end
			-- A harvested Beam/Trail records Attachment0/1 as {"Ref": "<full name>"},
			-- which is STRUCTURE, not a value. Rebuilt without an endpoints block it
			-- is a Beam wired to nothing: it builds, reports success and draws
			-- absolutely nothing. Skip it loudly rather than shipping a dead layer.
			if keep and (layer.class == "Beam" or layer.class == "Trail") and not layer.endpoints then
				keep = false
				skipped = skipped + 1
			end
			if keep then
				local att = Instance.new("Attachment")
				att.Name = e.id .. "_" .. layer.name .. "_" .. i
				-- The element offset goes on the ATTACHMENT only when the host is a
				-- parent part. An unparented recipe's host was already placed at
				-- anchor + offset, and adding it here as well put every such
				-- emitter at TWICE its authored offset. That shipped unnoticed
				-- because every effect had been tuned by eye against the doubled
				-- position. Authored offsets are now the true position. On a parent part
				-- the offset is in the part's LOCAL frame, so it turns with it.
				-- e.centred drops the LAYER's harvested offset. A pack records where
				-- each emitter's attachment sat, and some of those are STRUCTURE:
				-- Lava-01 is a beam effect whose layer #1 sits on the far end, 6.25
				-- studs out, and Lighting-01's Lightning layer hangs 9.9 up. Scaled
				-- with the effect, those put a stream's embers 15-27 studs from its
				-- own body. Opt-in, so every existing composition builds unchanged.
				local lo = e.centred and {0, 0, 0} or layer.offset
				att.Position = (e.parent and vec(e.offset) or Vector3.new()) + Vector3.new(
					(lo[1] or 0) * scale,
					(lo[2] or 0) * scale,
					(lo[3] or 0) * scale)
				att.Parent = host
				local inst = Instance.new(layer.class)
				inst.Name = layer.name
				for p, v in pairs(layer.props) do
					if type(v) ~= "table" or not v.Ref then
						local ok, dec = pcall(VFX.dec, v)
						if ok and dec ~= nil then pcall(function() inst[p] = dec end) end
					end
				end
				if scale ~= 1 then
					pcall(function() inst.Size = scaleSeq(inst.Size, scale) end)
					pcall(function() inst.Speed = NumberRange.new(inst.Speed.Min * scale, inst.Speed.Max * scale) end)
					pcall(function() inst.Acceleration = inst.Acceleration * scale end)
				end
				if e.tint then pcall(function() inst.Color = tintSeq(inst.Color, e.tint) end) end
				if e.lifetime_mul then pcall(function()
					inst.Lifetime = NumberRange.new(inst.Lifetime.Min * e.lifetime_mul, inst.Lifetime.Max * e.lifetime_mul)
				end) end
				if e.speed then pcall(function() inst.Speed = NumberRange.new(e.speed[1], e.speed[2]) end) end
				if e.spread then pcall(function() inst.SpreadAngle = Vector2.new(e.spread, e.spread) end) end
				if e.drag then pcall(function() inst.Drag = e.drag end) end
				if e.accel then pcall(function() inst.Acceleration = vec(e.accel) end) end
				if e.emission_dir then pcall(function() inst.EmissionDirection = Enum.NormalId[e.emission_dir] end) end
				if e.locked ~= nil then pcall(function() inst.LockedToPart = e.locked end) end
				if e.zoffset then pcall(function() inst.ZOffset = e.zoffset end) end
				-- The harvested count is a GUESS (Rate * 0.1). Overriding it per USE
				-- is most of the point of a composition: same recipe, right density.
				if inst:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then
					local em = layer.emit or {}
					local count = e.count or em.count or 20
					inst:SetAttribute("EmitCount", math.max(1, math.floor(count * (e.count_mul or 1))))
					-- A burst layer that also streams reads as "the effect never stops".
					if e.mode == "continuous" then
						-- rate_mul scales the rate the PACK used (harvested_rate survives
						-- a burst-mode harvest that zeroed Rate), so a streamed harvested
						-- effect keeps its authored density instead of a flat 20.
						local native = (em.harvested_rate and em.harvested_rate > 0 and em.harvested_rate)
							or ((inst.Rate and inst.Rate > 0) and inst.Rate) or 20
						inst.Rate = e.rate or (e.rate_mul and native * e.rate_mul) or native
						-- A harvested BURST streamed at its pack rate can be 1000/s.
						if e.rate_cap then inst.Rate = math.min(inst.Rate, e.rate_cap) end
						inst.Enabled = (e.start_enabled == true)
					else
						inst.Rate = 0
						inst.Enabled = false
					end
					inst.Parent = att
					table.insert(emitters, inst)
					table.insert(ALL_EMITTERS, inst)
				elseif inst:IsA("Beam") and layer.endpoints and #layer.endpoints >= 2 then
					-- A Beam INSIDE a recipe, wired from the endpoint offsets the harvester
					-- recorded (the aura rigs: a floor emitter with beams rising off it).
					-- Positions scale with the effect like every other offset; the width
					-- scales too or a shrunk aura keeps full-width beams.
					local base = e.parent and vec(e.offset) or Vector3.new()
					local ends = {}
					for k = 1, 2 do
						local o = layer.endpoints[k].offset or {0, 0, 0}
						local a = Instance.new("Attachment")
						a.Name = e.id .. "_" .. layer.name .. "_" .. i .. "_E" .. k
						a.Position = base + Vector3.new((o[1] or 0) * scale, (o[2] or 0) * scale, (o[3] or 0) * scale)
						a.Parent = host
						ends[k] = a
					end
					att:Destroy()
					inst.Attachment0 = ends[1]; inst.Attachment1 = ends[2]
					pcall(function() inst.Width0 = inst.Width0 * scale; inst.Width1 = inst.Width1 * scale end)
					inst.Enabled = false
					inst.Parent = host
					-- in el.emitters so enable/fade/hide reach it; NOT in ALL_EMITTERS,
					-- which the freeze walks setting TimeScale (a Beam has none)
					table.insert(emitters, inst)
				else
					att:Destroy()
					inst:Destroy()
					skipped = skipped + 1
				end
			end
		end
		return emitters, total, skipped
	end

	local function makeRing(el, e, host)
		local segs = {}
		local n = e.segments or 48
		for i = 1, n do
			local p = newPart("seg" .. i, host)
			p.Shape = Enum.PartType.Block
			p.Material = mat(e.material)
			p.Color = c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
			p.Transparency = e.transparency or 0
			table.insert(segs, p)
		end
		el.segs = segs
		el.n = n
		el.thick = e.thickness or 0.35
		el.height = e.height or 0.35
		el.center = anchorPos(e.anchor) + off(e.offset)
		el.tilt = e.tilt or 0
		el.spin = 0
		el.lastR = e.radius or 3
		el.setRadius = function(r, squash)
			el.lastR = r
			squash = squash or 1
			local arc = (2 * math.pi * r) / el.n
			for i, p in ipairs(el.segs) do
				local a = (i - 1) / el.n * math.pi * 2 + el.spin
				local dir = Vector3.new(math.cos(a), 0, math.sin(a))
				p.Size = Vector3.new(math.max(arc * 1.08, 0.05), el.height * squash, el.thick)
				local pos = el.center + dir * r
				p.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt(pos, pos + dir) * CFrame.Angles(math.rad(el.tilt), 0, 0)
			end
		end
		el.setRadius(el.lastR)
	end

	local function build(e)
		local el = { id = e.id, kind = e.kind, emitters = {} }
		-- An emitter on a MOVING host has to be parented to it. A fireball whose
		-- flames are pinned to the launch anchor is a fireball that leaves its own
		-- fire behind at the hand.
		local attachTo = nil
		if e.parent then
			local pe = EL[e.parent]
			if not pe then error("SCENE_ERROR element '" .. e.id .. "' parents to unbuilt '" .. tostring(e.parent) .. "'") end
			attachTo = pe.inst
			if not attachTo:IsA("BasePart") then
				error("SCENE_ERROR '" .. e.id .. "' parents to a " .. attachTo.ClassName .. ", needs a BasePart")
			end
		end
		if e.kind == "part" then
			local p = newPart(e.id, fx)
			p.Shape = Enum.PartType[e.shape or "Ball"]
			p.Size = vec(e.size or {1, 1, 1})
			p.Color = c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
			p.Material = mat(e.material)
			p.Transparency = e.transparency or 0
			local r = e.rot or {0, 0, 0}
			p.CFrame = CFrame.new(anchorPos(e.anchor) + off(e.offset)) * basis
				* CFrame.Angles(math.rad(r[1]), math.rad(r[2]), math.rad(r[3]))
			el.inst = p
			el.home = p.CFrame
			el.baseSize = p.Size
			if e.grow_from_bottom then el.bottom = p.Position.Y - p.Size.Y / 2 end
		elseif e.kind == "ring" then
			local m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = e.id; m.Parent = fx
			el.inst = m
			makeRing(el, e, m)
		elseif e.kind == "light" then
			local p = attachTo or newPart(e.id, fx)
			if not attachTo then
				p.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2); p.Transparency = 1
				p.CFrame = CFrame.new(anchorPos(e.anchor) + off(e.offset))
			end
			local l = Instance.new("PointLight")
			l.Color = c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
			l.Range = e.range or 24
			l.Brightness = e.brightness or 0
			l.Shadows = false
			l.Parent = p
			el.inst = p; el.light = l; el.home = p.CFrame
		elseif e.kind == "recipe" then
			local p = attachTo or newPart(e.id, fx)
			if not attachTo then
				p.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2); p.Transparency = 1
				p.CFrame = CFrame.new(anchorPos(e.anchor) + off(e.offset))
			end
			el.inst = p; el.home = p.CFrame
			local ems, total, skipped = buildRecipe(e, p)
			el.emitters = ems
			el.layerTotal = total
			el.skipped = skipped
		elseif e.kind == "group" then
			local m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = e.id; m.Parent = fx
			el.inst = m
			el.items = {}
			el.tangent = (e.orient == "tangent")
			local centre = anchorPos(e.anchor) + off(e.offset)
			el.centre = centre
			local n = e.count or 8
			local seed = Random.new(e.seed or 1234)
			local sz = e.size or {1, 1, 1}
			for i = 1, n do
				local p = newPart("i" .. i, m)
				p.Shape = Enum.PartType[e.shape or "Block"]
				p.Material = mat(e.material)
				p.Color = c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 1, 1))
				p.Transparency = e.transparency or 0
				local k = 1 + seed:NextNumber(-(e.size_jitter or 0), (e.size_jitter or 0))
				p.Size = Vector3.new(sz[1] * k, sz[2] * k, sz[3] * k)
				local a = (i - 1) / n * math.pi * 2 + (e.phase or 0)
				local rr = (e.radius or 4) * (1 + seed:NextNumber(-(e.radius_jitter or 0), (e.radius_jitter or 0)))
				-- y_ramp ties HEIGHT to the stagger order, which is what makes ice
				-- climb a body from the feet instead of appearing everywhere at once.
				local y
				if e.y_ramp then
					y = (e.y_min or 0) + ((e.y_max or 0) - (e.y_min or 0)) * ((i - 1) / math.max(n - 1, 1))
				else
					y = seed:NextNumber(e.y_min or 0, e.y_max or 0)
				end
				local tilt = e.tilt_jitter or 0
				-- local Z is the member's LONG axis; aim it radially OUTWARD so a
				-- long thin member reads as a crack running away from the centre.
				-- CFrame.Angles(0,-a,0) aims it tangentially - cracks then ran
				-- AROUND the circle instead of out of it.
				local yaw = (e.orient == "tangent") and -a or (math.pi / 2 - a)
				p.CFrame = CFrame.new(centre + Vector3.new(math.cos(a) * rr, y, math.sin(a) * rr))
					* CFrame.Angles(seed:NextNumber(-tilt, tilt), yaw, seed:NextNumber(-tilt, tilt))
				table.insert(el.items, {
					p = p, a0 = a, r0 = rr, y0 = y,
					rot = Vector3.new(seed:NextNumber(-4, 4), seed:NextNumber(-4, 4), seed:NextNumber(-4, 4)),
					vel = Vector3.new(seed:NextNumber(-1, 1), seed:NextNumber(0.3, 1.3), seed:NextNumber(-1, 1)).Unit,
					home = p.CFrame, size = p.Size, delay = (i - 1) / n,
				})
			end
		elseif e.kind == "bolt" then
			local m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = e.id; m.Parent = fx
			el.inst = m
			el.a = anchorPos(e.from) + off(e.from_offset)
			el.b = anchorPos(e.to) + off(e.to_offset)
			el.width = e.width or 0.6
			el.jitter = e.jitter or 3
			el.segments = e.segments or 14
			el.branches = e.branches or 4
			el.colour = c3(e.color, Color3.new(0.75, 0.85, 1))
			el.parts = {}
			el.regen = function(seed)
				for _, p in ipairs(el.parts) do p:Destroy() end
				el.parts = {}
				local rnd = Random.new(seed or 1)
				local function strand(a, b, w, jit, segs)
					local pts = { a }
					for i = 1, segs - 1 do
						local t = i / segs
						-- taper the wander to zero at both ends, or the bolt does not
						-- start and finish where it was aimed
						local envelope = math.sin(t * math.pi)
						table.insert(pts, a:Lerp(b, t) + Vector3.new(
							rnd:NextNumber(-jit, jit),
							rnd:NextNumber(-jit, jit) * 0.35,
							rnd:NextNumber(-jit, jit)) * envelope)
					end
					table.insert(pts, b)
					for i = 1, #pts - 1 do
						local p0, p1 = pts[i], pts[i + 1]
						local seg = newPart("b", m)
						seg.Shape = Enum.PartType.Block
						seg.Material = Enum.Material.Neon
						seg.Color = el.colour
						seg.Size = Vector3.new(w, w, (p1 - p0).Magnitude + w * 0.6)
						seg.CFrame = CFrame.lookAt((p0 + p1) / 2, p1)
						table.insert(el.parts, seg)
					end
					return pts
				end
				local main = strand(el.a, el.b, el.width, el.jitter, el.segments)
				local dir = (el.b - el.a).Unit
				-- Branch length is scaled to the BOLT, not fixed. Fixed-length
				-- branches on a 27-stud bolt sprawled 15 studs wide - wider than the
				-- main channel was tall on screen - and the strike point stopped
				-- being readable. A branch that outgrows its parent is a shrub.
				local span = (el.b - el.a).Magnitude
				local bmax = math.clamp(span * (el.branch_len or 0.16), 1.5, 9)
				for _ = 1, el.branches do
					local k = rnd:NextInteger(2, math.max(3, #main - 2))
					local from = main[k]
					-- taper: branches near the ground are shorter, like a real strike
					local taper = 0.35 + 0.65 * (1 - (k / #main))
					local tip = from + dir * rnd:NextNumber(bmax * 0.3, bmax * 0.8) * taper
						+ Vector3.new(rnd:NextNumber(-1, 1), rnd:NextNumber(-0.35, 0.1), rnd:NextNumber(-1, 1)).Unit
						* rnd:NextNumber(bmax * 0.35, bmax) * taper
					strand(from, tip, el.width * 0.45, el.jitter * 0.4, 4)
				end
			end
			el.regen(e.seed or 7)
			el.setTransparency = function(v)
				for _, p in ipairs(el.parts) do p.Transparency = v end
			end
		elseif e.kind == "trail" then
			-- A Trail is STRUCTURE, not values: it needs two live Attachments on the
			-- part it follows. This is the same reason a harvested Beam/Trail cannot
			-- be rebuilt from its recipe alone.
			if not attachTo then error("SCENE_ERROR trail '" .. e.id .. "' needs parent: <a part element>") end
			local a0 = Instance.new("Attachment"); a0.Name = e.id .. "_A0"
			local a1 = Instance.new("Attachment"); a1.Name = e.id .. "_A1"
			local w = (e.width or 1) * 0.5
			a0.Position = Vector3.new(0, w, 0); a1.Position = Vector3.new(0, -w, 0)
			a0.Parent = attachTo; a1.Parent = attachTo
			local tr = Instance.new("Trail")
			tr.Attachment0 = a0; tr.Attachment1 = a1
			tr.Lifetime = e.lifetime or 0.45
			tr.MinLength = 0
			tr.LightEmission = e.light_emission or 1
			tr.LightInfluence = 0
			tr.FaceCamera = true
			tr.Color = ColorSequence.new(c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 0.6, 0.2)), c3(e.color2, c3(e.color, Color3.new(1, 0.2, 0))))
			tr.Transparency = NumberSequence.new({
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(0, e.transparency or 0.1),
				NumberSequenceKeypoint.new(1, 1) })
			if e.texture then tr.Texture = e.texture end
			tr.Enabled = false
			tr.Parent = attachTo
			el.inst = attachTo; el.trail = tr
		elseif e.kind == "chain" then
			-- ONE harvested recipe strung at `points` hosts between two anchors, so
			-- a line (a lightning bolt, a crackling tether) is drawn by the harvest's
			-- own effects instead of Neon segments. Positions come from the engine's
			-- anchors, so the line is right in game as well as on the edit stage.
			local a = anchorPos(e.from) + off(e.from_offset)
			local b = anchorPos(e.to) + off(e.to_offset)
			local m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = e.id; m.Parent = fx
			el.inst = m
			local rnd = Random.new(e.seed or 3)
			local n = math.max(1, e.points or 5)
			local j = e.jitter or 0
			for k = 1, n do
				local tt = (n == 1) and 0.5 or (k - 1) / (n - 1)
				local p = newPart(e.id .. "_" .. k, m)
				p.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2); p.Transparency = 1
				local jit = Vector3.new(rnd:NextNumber(-j, j), rnd:NextNumber(-j, j) * 0.5, rnd:NextNumber(-j, j))
				if k == 1 or k == n then jit = Vector3.new() end
				local pos = a:Lerp(b, tt) + jit
				p.CFrame = (b - a).Magnitude > 1e-3 and CFrame.lookAt(pos, b) or CFrame.new(pos)
				local ems = buildRecipe(e, p)
				for _, em in ipairs(ems) do table.insert(el.emitters, em) end
			end
		elseif e.kind == "beam" then
			-- A HARVESTED Beam layer stretched between two points. A pack's Beam
			-- records Attachment0/1 as {"Ref"}, which is structure, so buildRecipe
			-- skips it (a Beam wired to nothing draws nothing). This kind supplies
			-- the structure: one layer, two attachments, each on an anchor or on a
			-- moving part element (parent / to_parent), so a beam can follow a
			-- projectile. Until 2026-09-10 no Beam in any harvested pack could be
			-- used at all - the wind, lava, waterfall and aura beams were dead weight.
			local rec = comp.recipes[e.recipe]
			if not rec then error("SCENE_ERROR recipe not inlined: " .. tostring(e.recipe)) end
			local want = tostring(e.layer or "#1")
			local idx = string.match(want, "^#(%d+)$")
			local layer
			for i, l in ipairs(rec.layers) do
				if (idx and i == tonumber(idx)) or (not idx and l.name == want) then layer = l; break end
			end
			if not layer or layer.class ~= "Beam" then
				error("SCENE_ERROR beam '" .. e.id .. "': layer " .. want .. " of " .. e.recipe .. " is not a Beam")
			end
			local function endPart(anchor, o, parentId, tag)
				if parentId then
					local pe = EL[parentId]
					if not pe or not pe.inst:IsA("BasePart") then
						error("SCENE_ERROR beam '" .. e.id .. "' end parents to unbuilt/non-part '" .. tostring(parentId) .. "'")
					end
					return pe.inst
				end
				local p = newPart(e.id .. tag, fx)
				p.Size = Vector3.new(0.2, 0.2, 0.2); p.Transparency = 1
				p.CFrame = CFrame.new(anchorPos(anchor) + off(o)) * basis
				return p
			end
			local pa = endPart(e.from, e.from_offset, e.parent, "_A")
			local pb = endPart(e.to, e.to_offset, e.to_parent, "_B")
			local a0 = Instance.new("Attachment"); a0.Name = e.id .. "_A0"; a0.Parent = pa
			local a1 = Instance.new("Attachment"); a1.Name = e.id .. "_A1"; a1.Parent = pb
			local b = Instance.new("Beam")
			for p, v in pairs(layer.props) do
				if type(v) ~= "table" or not v.Ref then
					local ok, dec = pcall(VFX.dec, v)
					if ok and dec ~= nil then pcall(function() b[p] = dec end) end
				end
			end
			b.Attachment0 = a0; b.Attachment1 = a1
			local wm = e.width_mul or 1
			pcall(function() b.Width0 = b.Width0 * wm; b.Width1 = b.Width1 * wm end)
			if e.tint then pcall(function() b.Color = tintSeq(b.Color, e.tint) end) end
			if e.segments then b.Segments = e.segments end
			b.Enabled = false
			b.Name = e.id
			b.Parent = pa
			el.inst = pa; el.home = pa.CFrame; el.beam = b
		elseif e.kind == "clone" or e.kind == "model" then
			-- clone: a frozen copy of a stage model, recoloured (the blink afterimage)
			-- model: the LIVE stage model, so the character itself can be faded out
			local src = ctx.sourceModel(e.source)
			if not src then error("SCENE_ERROR no source model '" .. tostring(e.source) .. "'") end
			local m = src
			if e.kind == "clone" then
				-- COPY THE PARTS, DO NOT Clone() THE MODEL. Against a stage dummy a
				-- whole-model Clone is fine; against a LIVE PLAYER CHARACTER it is
				-- not. Clone() returns NIL for a non-archivable instance, and the
				-- very next line indexes it, so the error killed the entire
				-- composition and the effect showed nothing at all - while every
				-- effect that does not clone kept working. A whole-model clone also
				-- drags in a second Humanoid, the Animate script and every
				-- accessory, none of which a silhouette wants.
				--
				-- A silhouette is SHAPE ONLY, so copy the BaseParts and keep just
				-- their meshes.
				m = Instance.new("Model"); m.Name = e.id; m.Parent = fx
				local shift = e.offset and off(e.offset) or Vector3.new()
				for _, d in ipairs(src:GetDescendants()) do
					if d:IsA("BasePart") and d.Transparency < 1 then
						d.Archivable = true
						local okc, c = pcall(function() return d:Clone() end)
						if okc and c then
							for _, ch in ipairs(c:GetChildren()) do
								if not ch:IsA("DataModelMesh") then ch:Destroy() end
							end
							c.Anchored = true; c.CanCollide = false; c.CanQuery = false
							c.CanTouch = false; c.CastShadow = false; c.Massless = true
							c.CFrame = d.CFrame + shift
							c.Parent = m
						end
					end
				end
				if #m:GetChildren() == 0 then
					error("SCENE_ERROR clone '" .. e.id .. "' copied no parts from " .. src:GetFullName())
				end
			end
			el.inst = m
			el.parts = {}
			for _, d in ipairs(m:GetDescendants()) do
				if d:IsA("BasePart") then
					-- base is what the part looked like BEFORE this element touched
					-- it. Capturing it afterwards means a clone authored as
					-- transparency 1 records base=1, the "keep genuinely invisible
					-- parts invisible" guard then rejects every part, and the clone
					-- can NEVER be faded back in. The ghost was unrenderable.
					local base = d.Transparency
					if e.kind == "clone" then
						d.Anchored = true; d.CanCollide = false; d.CanQuery = false
						-- Recolour ONLY when asked. A clone with its own look is the
						-- arriving character; a recoloured one is the afterimage.
						if e.material then d.Material = mat(e.material) end
						if e.color then d.Color = c3(e.color) end
						if e.transparency and base < 1 then d.Transparency = e.transparency end
					end
					table.insert(el.parts, { p = d, base = base })
				end
			end
			el.setTransparency = function(v)
				for _, r in ipairs(el.parts) do
					-- an already-invisible part (HumanoidRootPart) must STAY invisible
					if r.base < 1 then r.p.Transparency = v end
				end
			end
		else
			error("SCENE_ERROR unknown element kind '" .. tostring(e.kind) .. "'")
		end
		EL[e.id] = el
		return el
	end

	-- Build each element in its own pcall. One bad element used to throw out of
	-- the loop and take the WHOLE composition with it, so a single unbuildable
	-- piece read as "that effect does nothing" with no clue which piece. Report
	-- and carry on: a partial effect is debuggable, an absent one is not.
	local buildErrors = {}
	for _, e in ipairs(comp.elements) do
		local okb, errb = pcall(build, e)
		if not okb then
			table.insert(buildErrors, e.id .. ": " .. tostring(errb))
			warn("[VFX] " .. comp.name .. " element '" .. e.id .. "' FAILED: " .. tostring(errb))
		end
	end

	-- Snapshot AFTER every element exists, so replaying a scene starts from the
	-- authored look rather than from wherever the previous run left it.
	for _, e in ipairs(comp.elements) do
		local el = EL[e.id] or { kind = "__failed" }   -- its build error was already reported
		local t = e.transparency or 0
		if el.kind == "ring" then
			local r = el.lastR
			table.insert(INITIAL, function()
				el.spin = 0; el.setRadius(r)
				for _, p in ipairs(el.segs) do p.Transparency = t end
			end)
		elseif el.kind == "group" then
			local snap = {}
			for i, it in ipairs(el.items) do snap[i] = { cf = it.p.CFrame, sz = it.p.Size } end
			table.insert(INITIAL, function()
				for i, it in ipairs(el.items) do
					it.p.CFrame = snap[i].cf; it.p.Size = snap[i].sz; it.p.Transparency = t
				end
			end)
		elseif el.kind == "part" then
			local cf, sz = el.home, el.baseSize
			table.insert(INITIAL, function() el.inst.CFrame = cf; el.inst.Size = sz; el.inst.Transparency = t end)
		elseif el.kind == "light" then
			table.insert(INITIAL, function() el.light.Brightness = e.brightness or 0 end)
		elseif el.kind == "bolt" or el.kind == "clone" or el.kind == "model" then
			table.insert(INITIAL, function() el.setTransparency(t) end)
		elseif el.kind == "trail" then
			table.insert(INITIAL, function() el.trail.Enabled = false end)
		elseif el.kind == "beam" then
			local cf = el.home
			table.insert(INITIAL, function() el.beam.Enabled = false; el.inst.CFrame = cf end)
		end
	end

	local function setAlpha(el, v)
		if el.kind == "ring" then for _, p in ipairs(el.segs) do p.Transparency = v end
		elseif el.kind == "bolt" or el.kind == "clone" or el.kind == "model" then el.setTransparency(v)
		elseif el.kind == "group" then for _, it in ipairs(el.items) do it.p.Transparency = v end
		elseif el.kind == "trail" then el.trail.Enabled = v < 0.99
		elseif el.kind == "beam" then el.beam.Enabled = v < 0.99
		elseif el.kind == "recipe" or el.kind == "chain" then
			for _, em in ipairs(el.emitters) do pcall(function() em.Enabled = v < 0.99 end) end
		else el.inst.Transparency = v end
	end

	-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- timeline
	-- Every cue is either an INSTANT (emit/enable/destroy/regen/hide/show) or a
	-- TRACK with a start, a duration and an apply(alpha). Nothing uses TweenService:
	-- a tween cannot be frozen mid-flight, only cancelled, and cancelling loses the
	-- pose - which would make phase-frozen capture impossible for everything except
	-- the particles.
	local tracks, cues = {}, {}
	for _, c in ipairs(comp.timeline) do
		local el = EL[c.id]
		if not el then
			-- its element failed to build; skip the cue rather than compounding
			warn("[VFX] " .. comp.name .. " cue skipped, no element '" .. tostring(c.id) .. "'")
			el = nil
		end
		if el then
		local a = c.act
		if a == "emit" or a == "enable" or a == "destroy" or a == "regen" or a == "hide"
			or a == "show" or a == "warp" then
			table.insert(cues, c)
		else
			local f = ease(c.style)
			local t0, dur = c.t or 0, c.time or 0.5
			local apply
			if a == "scale" then
				local from, to = c.from or 0.01, c.to or 1
				apply = function(al)
					local k = from + (to - from) * f(al)
					local p = el.inst
					p.Size = el.baseSize * k
					if el.bottom then
						p.CFrame = CFrame.new(el.home.Position.X, el.bottom + p.Size.Y / 2, el.home.Position.Z)
							* (el.home - el.home.Position)
					end
				end
			elseif a == "radius" then
				local from, to = c.from or 0.5, c.to or 10
				apply = function(al)
					local k = f(al)
					el.setRadius(from + (to - from) * k, c.squash_to and (1 + (c.squash_to - 1) * k) or 1)
				end
			elseif a == "fade" then
				local from, to = c.from or 0, c.to or 1
				apply = function(al) setAlpha(el, from + (to - from) * f(al)) end
			elseif a == "light" then
				local from, to = c.from or 0, c.to or 0
				apply = function(al) el.light.Brightness = from + (to - from) * f(al) end
			elseif a == "spin" then
				local dps = c.deg_per_sec or 90
				apply = function(al)
					local ang = math.rad(dps * dur * al)
					if el.kind == "ring" then
						el.spin = ang; el.setRadius(el.lastR)
					elseif el.kind == "group" then
						for _, it in ipairs(el.items) do
							local a2 = it.a0 + ang
							it.p.CFrame = CFrame.new(el.centre
								+ Vector3.new(math.cos(a2) * it.r0, it.y0, math.sin(a2) * it.r0))
								* CFrame.Angles(0, el.tangent and -a2 or (math.pi / 2 - a2), 0)
						end
					else
						el.inst.CFrame = el.home * CFrame.Angles(0, ang, 0)
					end
				end
			elseif a == "fly" then
				local to = anchorPos(c.to) + off(c.to_offset)
				local arc = c.arc or 0
				apply = function(al)
					local k = f(al)
					local pos = el.home.Position:Lerp(to, k) + Vector3.new(0, math.sin(k * math.pi) * arc, 0)
					el.inst.CFrame = CFrame.new(pos) * (el.home - el.home.Position)
				end
			elseif a == "spiral" then
				local r1 = c.to_radius or 0
				local turns = c.turns or 2
				apply = function(al)
					local k = f(al)
					for _, it in ipairs(el.items) do
						local r = it.r0 + (r1 - it.r0) * k
						local ang = it.a0 + turns * math.pi * 2 * k
						it.p.CFrame = CFrame.new(el.centre + Vector3.new(math.cos(ang) * r, it.y0 * (1 - k), math.sin(ang) * r))
							* CFrame.Angles(it.rot.X * k * 6, it.rot.Y * k * 6, it.rot.Z * k * 6)
						if c.shrink then it.p.Size = it.size * math.max(1 - k * c.shrink, 0.02) end
					end
				end
			elseif a == "burst" then
				local speed = c.speed or 20
				local g = c.gravity or 60
				apply = function(al)
					local tt = al * dur
					for _, it in ipairs(el.items) do
						local d = it.vel * speed * tt - Vector3.new(0, 0.5 * g * tt * tt, 0)
						it.p.CFrame = CFrame.new(it.home.Position + d)
							* CFrame.Angles(it.rot.X * tt * 3, it.rot.Y * tt * 3, it.rot.Z * tt * 3)
					end
				end
			elseif a == "stagger" then
				-- every member runs the SAME sub-animation, offset in time. This is
				-- what makes ice climb a body and rune symbols light in sequence.
				local spread = c.spread or 0.5
				local from, to = c.from or 0.01, c.to or 1
				apply = function(al)
					for _, it in ipairs(el.items) do
						local la = math.clamp((al * dur - it.delay * spread) / math.max(dur - spread, 0.05), 0, 1)
						local k = from + (to - from) * f(la)
						it.p.Size = it.size * k
						if c.from_bottom then
							it.p.CFrame = CFrame.new(it.home.Position.X,
								it.home.Position.Y - it.size.Y / 2 + it.p.Size.Y / 2,
								it.home.Position.Z) * (it.home - it.home.Position)
						end
					end
				end
			elseif a == "move" then
				local to = anchorPos(c.to) + off(c.to_offset)
				apply = function(al)
					local k = f(al)
					if el.kind == "ring" then el.center = el.center:Lerp(to, 0); el.center = (el.homeCentre or el.center)
					else el.inst.CFrame = CFrame.new(el.home.Position:Lerp(to, k)) * (el.home - el.home.Position) end
				end
			end
			if apply then
				-- Park at frame zero ONLY for tracks that start at t=0. Applying a
				-- LATER track's alpha-0 state at build time overwrites the element's
				-- authored state: the fireball's impact ring has a fade track
				-- starting at t=1.02 with from=0.1, so apply(0) made it visible on
				-- the ground from the first frame, a third of the flight before the
				-- fireball arrived.
				table.insert(tracks, { t0 = t0, dur = dur, apply = apply, done = false, park = t0 <= 0 })
				if t0 <= 0 then apply(0) end
			end
		end
		end
	end
	table.sort(cues, function(x, y) return (x.t or 0) < (y.t or 0) end)

	local function fireCue(c)
		local el = EL[c.id]
		if c.act == "emit" then
			for _, em in ipairs(el.emitters) do
				if em:IsA("ParticleEmitter") then
					em:Emit(math.max(1, math.floor((em:GetAttribute("EmitCount") or 20) * (c.mult or 1))))
				elseif em:IsA("Beam") then
					-- a burst's beam has no count; it shows for the element's beam_hold
					em.Enabled = true
						task.delay(c.beam_hold or 0.35, function() if em.Parent then em.Enabled = false end end)
				end
			end
		elseif c.act == "enable" then
			if el.trail then el.trail.Enabled = c.on ~= false end
			if el.beam then el.beam.Enabled = c.on ~= false end
			for _, em in ipairs(el.emitters) do pcall(function() em.Enabled = c.on ~= false end) end
		elseif c.act == "regen" then
			el.regen(c.seed or math.random(1, 99999))
		elseif c.act == "hide" then
			setAlpha(el, 1)
		elseif c.act == "show" then
			setAlpha(el, c.to or 0)
		elseif c.act == "warp" then
			-- Move a model outright. A blink that leaves you standing where you
			-- started is not a blink; in game this is the act that actually
			-- relocates the player. Keep the pivot's height ABOVE THE MODEL'S
			-- BASE, not the pivot's absolute Y - a character's pivot sits at the
			-- HumanoidRootPart, so warping to a ground point would bury it.
			local m = el.inst
			if m and m:IsA("Model") then
				local to = anchorPos(c.to) + off(c.to_offset)
				local pivot = m:GetPivot()
				local bcf, bsize = m:GetBoundingBox()
				local lift = pivot.Position.Y - (bcf.Position.Y - bsize.Y / 2)
				m:PivotTo(CFrame.new(to.X, to.Y + lift, to.Z) * (pivot - pivot.Position))
			end
		elseif c.act == "destroy" then
			el.inst:Destroy()
		end
	end

	-- Generation guard. Without it a second play() runs CONCURRENTLY with the first
	-- and they fight over every property: the payload builds and plays through, you
	-- then ask for a frozen phase, and the still-running first loop keeps stepping
	-- the tracks to the end. It reports FROZEN at the time you asked for while the
	-- scene on screen is the end state - a green message over a wrong picture.
	local generation = 0

	local function play(freeze)
		generation = generation + 1
		local mine = generation
		-- Restore every element's AUTHORED look first, then park only the t=0
		-- tracks. Replaying without this leaves the previous run's end state on any
		-- element whose tracks all start late.
		for _, r in ipairs(INITIAL) do pcall(r) end
		for _, tr in ipairs(tracks) do
			tr.done = false
			if tr.park then pcall(tr.apply, 0) end
		end
		for _, em in ipairs(ALL_EMITTERS) do
			pcall(function() em.TimeScale = 1; em:Clear(); em.Enabled = false end)
		end
		task.spawn(function()
			local fired = {}
			local t0 = os.clock()
			while generation == mine do
				local now = os.clock() - t0
				local tt = (freeze >= 0) and math.min(now, freeze) or now
				for i, c in ipairs(cues) do
					if not fired[i] and (c.t or 0) <= tt then fired[i] = true; pcall(fireCue, c) end
				end
				for _, tr in ipairs(tracks) do
					if tt >= tr.t0 then
						local al = (tr.dur <= 0) and 1 or math.clamp((tt - tr.t0) / tr.dur, 0, 1)
						if al < 1 or not tr.done then pcall(tr.apply, al) end
						if al >= 1 then tr.done = true end
					end
				end
				if freeze >= 0 and now >= freeze then break end
				if now > (comp.duration or 4) + 0.6 then break end
				task.wait()
			end
			if generation ~= mine then return end   -- superseded; do not touch anything
			-- Phase freeze: a burst lasts under a second, so an unfrozen screenshot
			-- is a coin flip. TimeScale = 0 holds the exact phase until it is reset.
			if freeze >= 0 then
				for _, em in ipairs(ALL_EMITTERS) do pcall(function() em.TimeScale = 0 end) end
			end
			ctx.report(string.format("FROZEN %s t=%.2f gen=%d emitters=%d tracks=%d cues=%d",
				comp.name, freeze, mine, #ALL_EMITTERS, #tracks, #cues))
			if ctx.onFinish then pcall(ctx.onFinish, freeze) end
		end)
	end

	local built = {}
	for _, e in ipairs(comp.elements) do
		local el = EL[e.id]
		local d = e.kind
		if el.emitters and #el.emitters > 0 then
			d = d .. "(" .. #el.emitters .. "/" .. (el.layerTotal or 0) .. "L"
				.. ((el.skipped or 0) > 0 and (" -" .. el.skipped .. "unwirable") or "") .. ")"
		end
		table.insert(built, e.id .. ":" .. d)
	end
	ctx.report("built " .. comp.name .. " :: " .. table.concat(built, ", "))

	return {
		name = comp.name,
		duration = comp.duration or 3,
		play = play,
		stop = function() generation = generation + 1 end,
		built = built,
		elements = EL,
		emitters = ALL_EMITTERS,
	}
end

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check recipe JSON for defects that a screenshot will not show you.

This does NOT judge whether an effect looks good. Nothing here can. It catches
the failures that are invisible in a still: a truncated property set, an emitter
that is transparent for its whole life, a burst layer that also streams forever,
a texture path that renders as nothing.

Run --self-test to prove the checks can actually fail. A verifier that has never
been shown to fail is a verifier that says yes.
"""
import argparse
import copy
import json
import os
import pathlib
import sys

def default_lib():
    """Your recipe folder: --lib or the ROBLOX_VFX_LIB env var (see LOCAL.md)."""
    v = os.environ.get("ROBLOX_VFX_LIB")
    if not v and (pathlib.Path.home() / "Roblox-VFX-Library").is_dir():
        v = str(pathlib.Path.home() / "Roblox-VFX-Library")  # the setup skill's default
    if not v:
        sys.exit("no recipe library given: pass --lib <your VFX library folder> "
                 "or set ROBLOX_VFX_LIB (the path is in LOCAL.md)")
    p = pathlib.Path(v).expanduser()
    return p / "recipes" if (p / "recipes").is_dir() else p

# MEASURED in Studio 2026-08-26 by probing a live ParticleEmitter, not read off
# the docs. The MCP's generic property reader returns 6 of these 31.
PE_PROPS = {
    "Acceleration", "Brightness", "Color", "Drag", "EmissionDirection", "Enabled",
    "FlipbookFramerate", "FlipbookLayout", "FlipbookMode", "FlipbookStartRandom",
    "Lifetime", "LightEmission", "LightInfluence", "LockedToPart", "Orientation",
    "Rate", "RotSpeed", "Rotation", "Shape", "ShapeInOut", "ShapeStyle", "Size",
    "SpreadAngle", "Speed", "Squash", "Texture", "TimeScale", "Transparency",
    "VelocityInheritance", "ZOffset", "WindAffectsDrag",
}
LIGHT_PROPS = {"Brightness", "Color", "Enabled", "Range", "Shadows"}

# MEASURED by rendering each one, 2026-08-27. FIVE stock paths exist, not the
# three this file claimed until a real pack was harvested: the first pass only
# probed textures/particles/*.dds and never looked in textures/ itself, so two
# live paths were being hard-failed as nonexistent.
STOCK_TEXTURES = {
    "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds",
    "rbxasset://textures/particles/fire_main.dds",
    "rbxasset://textures/particles/smoke_main.dds",
    "rbxasset://textures/explosion.png",   # puffy lit explosion cloud
    "rbxasset://textures/sparkle.png",     # hard 8-point star, dark rim
}

# MEASURED to render NOTHING despite looking exactly as plausible as the five
# above. textures/smoke.png is the trap: Roblox's OWN "Particle Effects" pack
# (228304820) ships a Smoke layer pointing at it, so a first-party pack contains
# a permanently invisible emitter. Named explicitly to make the failure legible
# rather than a generic "not in the stock set".
KNOWN_DEAD_TEXTURES = {
    "rbxasset://textures/smoke.png",
    "rbxasset://textures/fire.png",
    "rbxasset://textures/particle.png",
}

KNOWN_CLASSES = {"ParticleEmitter", "Beam", "Trail", "PointLight"}



def recipes_dir(p) -> pathlib.Path:
    """A library ROOT holds recipes/, index.json and harvested/; accept either it or recipes/."""
    p = pathlib.Path(p).expanduser().resolve()
    return p / "recipes" if (p / "recipes").is_dir() else p

def seq(props, key):
    v = props.get(key)
    if isinstance(v, dict) and "NumberSequence" in v:
        return v["NumberSequence"]
    return None


def check(recipe):
    """Return a list of (severity, message). severity in {'fail','warn'}."""
    out = []
    name = recipe.get("name", "<unnamed>")
    layers = recipe.get("layers") or []

    if not layers:
        out.append(("fail", f"{name}: no layers"))
        return out

    # One emitter is almost never an effect. Worth saying out loud.
    emitters = [L for L in layers if L.get("class") == "ParticleEmitter"]
    if len(emitters) == 1:
        out.append(("warn", f"{name}: a single ParticleEmitter rarely reads as an effect; "
                            "real ones layer a core, a body and sparks"))

    max_life = 0.0
    for L in layers:
        ln = f"{name}.{L.get('name','?')}"
        cls = L.get("class")
        props = L.get("props") or {}
        emit = L.get("emit") or {}

        if cls not in KNOWN_CLASSES:
            out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: unknown class {cls!r}"))
            continue

        if cls == "ParticleEmitter":
            missing = PE_PROPS - set(props)
            if missing:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: {len(missing)} of {len(PE_PROPS)} properties missing "
                                    f"({', '.join(sorted(missing)[:6])}"
                                    f"{'...' if len(missing) > 6 else ''}) - harvested through a "
                                    "generic property reader instead of an explicit walk?"))

            tex = props.get("Texture")
            if not tex:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: no Texture"))
            elif isinstance(tex, str) and tex in KNOWN_DEAD_TEXTURES:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: {tex} renders as NOTHING (measured). It looks like a "
                                    "real path and Roblox's own packs ship it; this emitter costs "
                                    "budget and draws nothing"))
            elif isinstance(tex, str) and tex.startswith("rbxasset://") and tex not in STOCK_TEXTURES:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: {tex} is not one of the {len(STOCK_TEXTURES)} stock "
                                    "textures measured to exist; a wrong rbxasset path renders as "
                                    "nothing, with no error"))

            rate = props.get("Rate")
            mode = emit.get("mode")
            if mode == "burst" and rate not in (0, 0.0):
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: burst layer has Rate={rate}; it will stream forever "
                                    "as well as bursting"))
            if mode == "continuous" and (rate in (0, 0.0) or rate is None):
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: continuous layer has Rate={rate}; it will never emit"))
            if mode == "burst" and not emit.get("count"):
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: burst layer has no emit count"))

            life = props.get("Lifetime", {}).get("NumberRange")
            if not life or life[0] <= 0 or life[1] < life[0]:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: bad Lifetime {life}"))
            else:
                max_life = max(max_life, life[1])

            tr = seq(props, "Transparency")
            if tr is not None:
                if all(kp[1] >= 0.999 for kp in tr):
                    out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: Transparency is 1 across the whole life; "
                                        "this emitter costs budget and draws nothing"))
                if min(kp[1] for kp in tr) > 0.95:
                    out.append(("warn", f"{ln}: never gets more opaque than "
                                        f"{min(kp[1] for kp in tr):.2f}; may be invisible in play"))

            sz = seq(props, "Size")
            if sz is not None and all(kp[1] <= 0.0001 for kp in sz):
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: Size is 0 across the whole life"))

            for key in ("Size", "Transparency", "Squash"):
                s = seq(props, key)
                if s is None:
                    continue
                times = [kp[0] for kp in s]
                if abs(times[0]) > 1e-6 or abs(times[-1] - 1) > 1e-6:
                    out.append(("fail", f"{ln}.{key}: NumberSequence must span t=0..1, got "
                                        f"{times[0]}..{times[-1]}"))
                if any(b < a for a, b in zip(times, times[1:])):
                    out.append(("fail", f"{ln}.{key}: keypoint times are not ascending"))

        elif cls in ("Beam", "Trail"):
            eps = L.get("endpoints")
            if not eps or len(eps) != 2:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: a {cls} needs two endpoints; without both "
                                    "attachments wired it builds fine and draws nothing"))
            elif any(e.get("missing") for e in eps):
                out.append(("warn", f"{ln}: an endpoint was unresolved in the source pack "
                                    "and got a default offset; check the length looks right"))

        elif cls == "PointLight":
            missing = LIGHT_PROPS - set(props)
            if missing:
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: missing light properties {sorted(missing)}"))
            if emit.get("mode") == "pulse" and not emit.get("from"):
                out.append(("fail", f"{ln}: pulse light has no peak brightness ('from')"))

    inferred = [L.get("name", "?") for L in layers if (L.get("emit") or {}).get("inferred")]
    if inferred:
        out.append(("warn", f"{name}: emit mode was INFERRED for {len(inferred)} layer(s) "
                            f"({', '.join(inferred[:4])}{'...' if len(inferred) > 4 else ''}). "
                            "A harvested pack records no burst window, so the counts are a guess. "
                            "Preview it before indexing."))

    stranded = [L.get("name", "?") for L in layers if L.get("renders_in_place") is False]
    if stranded:
        out.append(("warn", f"{name}: {len(stranded)} layer(s) were parented to a "
                            f"{layers[0].get('parent_class')} in the source pack "
                            f"({', '.join(stranded[:4])}), so they render NOTHING where they sit. "
                            "Harvested fine; rebuild puts them on a BasePart."))

    dur = recipe.get("duration")
    if dur is not None and max_life and dur < max_life:
        out.append(("warn", f"{name}: duration {dur}s is shorter than its longest particle "
                            f"life {max_life:.2f}s; previews will cut the tail off"))

    texs = recipe.get("texture_refs") or []
    portable = recipe.get("texture_portable")
    # No texture refs at all = nothing to depend on = portable. This used to be
    # hardcoded False, which made every textureless Beam fail against the sink's
    # (correct) all([]) == True.
    actually = all(t.startswith("rbxasset://") for t in texs)
    if portable is not None and portable != actually:
        out.append(("fail", f"{name}: texture_portable={portable} but refs say {actually}"))
    if texs and not actually:
        out.append(("warn", f"{name}: depends on non-stock texture assets; these may not render "
                            "in another place or for another owner"))
    return out


def run(paths, quiet=False):
    fails = warns = 0
    clean = 0
    for p in paths:
        rec = json.loads(p.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        res = check(rec)
        f = sum(1 for s, _ in res if s == "fail")
        w = len(res) - f
        fails += f
        warns += w
        status = "FAIL" if f else ("warn" if w else "ok")
        if status == "ok":
            clean += 1
        if quiet and status != "FAIL":
            continue
        print(f"[{status:4s}] {p.name}  ({len(rec.get('layers', []))} layers)")
        for sev, msg in res:
            if quiet and sev != "fail":
                continue
            print(f"         {sev}: {msg}")
    print(f"\n{len(paths)} recipe(s): {clean} clean, {fails} failure(s), {warns} warning(s)")
    return 1 if fails else 0


SABOTAGES = [
    ("drop 5 properties",
     lambda r: [r["layers"][0]["props"].pop(k, None)
                for k in ("Rate", "Speed", "Drag", "Texture", "Lifetime")]),
    # Must set BOTH, or on a continuous layer a nonzero Rate is simply correct
    # and there is nothing for the check to find.
    ("burst layer that also streams",
     lambda r: (r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__("Rate", 25),
                r["layers"][0].__setitem__("emit", {"mode": "burst", "count": 12}))),
    ("continuous layer that never emits",
     lambda r: (r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__("Rate", 0),
                r["layers"][0].__setitem__("emit", {"mode": "continuous"}))),
    ("texture path that does not exist",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__(
         "Texture", "rbxasset://textures/particles/explosion01_smoke1.dds")),
    ("plausible path measured to render nothing",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__(
         "Texture", "rbxasset://textures/smoke.png")),
    ("fully transparent emitter",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__(
         "Transparency", {"NumberSequence": [[0, 1, 0], [1, 1, 0]]})),
    ("sequence that does not span 0..1",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__(
         "Size", {"NumberSequence": [[0.2, 1, 0], [0.8, 2, 0]]})),
    ("negative lifetime",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0]["props"].__setitem__("Lifetime", {"NumberRange": [-1, 0]})),
    ("portability flag lying about the refs",
     lambda r: (r.__setitem__("texture_refs", ["rbxassetid://12345"]),
                r.__setitem__("texture_portable", True))),
    ("unknown layer class",
     lambda r: r["layers"][0].__setitem__("class", "Sparkles")),
]


def _demo_recipe():
    """A minimal valid recipe, built in code, for --self-test.

    No effects ship with this skill, so the self-test cannot borrow one from a
    library. It needs a baseline that passes every check, so each sabotage proves
    one check can fail."""
    tex = "rbxasset://textures/particles/sparkles_main.dds"
    props = {k: 0 for k in PE_PROPS}
    props.update({
        "Texture": tex,
        "Rate": 0,
        "Lifetime": {"NumberRange": [0.5, 1.0]},
        "Transparency": {"NumberSequence": [[0, 0, 0], [1, 1, 0]]},
        "Size": {"NumberSequence": [[0, 1, 0], [1, 0.2, 0]]},
        "Squash": {"NumberSequence": [[0, 0, 0], [1, 0, 0]]},
        "Enabled": False,
    })
    layer = {"name": "Core", "class": "ParticleEmitter", "offset": [0, 0, 0],
             "emit": {"mode": "burst", "count": 12}, "props": props}
    return {"name": "SelfTestDemo", "duration": 1.5, "texture_portable": True,
            "texture_refs": [tex], "layers": [layer, json.loads(json.dumps(layer))]}


def self_test():
    base = _demo_recipe()

    clean = check(base)
    clean_fails = [m for s, m in clean if s == "fail"]
    print(f"baseline {base['name']}: {len(clean_fails)} failure(s)")
    if clean_fails:
        for m in clean_fails:
            print(f"   fail: {m}")
        print("SELF-TEST INVALID: baseline recipe does not pass")
        return 1

    bad = 0
    for label, mutate in SABOTAGES:
        r = copy.deepcopy(base)
        # sabotage the first ParticleEmitter, not whatever is at index 0
        i = next(i for i, L in enumerate(r["layers"]) if L["class"] == "ParticleEmitter")
        r["layers"][0], r["layers"][i] = r["layers"][i], r["layers"][0]
        mutate(r)
        res = [m for s, m in check(r) if s == "fail"]
        ok = bool(res)
        print(f"  [{'caught' if ok else 'MISSED'}] {label}")
        if ok:
            print(f"            -> {res[0]}")
        else:
            bad += 1
    print(f"\nself-test: {len(SABOTAGES) - bad}/{len(SABOTAGES)} sabotages caught")
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("recipes", nargs="*")
    ap.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
    # Your harvested library lives OUTSIDE the skill directory, so updating or
    # sharing the skill can never carry an extracted pack with it.
    ap.add_argument("--lib", default=None,
                    help="recipe directory (default: $ROBLOX_VFX_LIB, your own library)")
    ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true",
                    help="one line per recipe, failures only")
    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.self_test:
        sys.exit(self_test())
    lib = recipes_dir(a.lib) if a.lib else default_lib()
    paths = [pathlib.Path(x) for x in a.recipes] or sorted(lib.glob("*.json"))
    if not paths:
        print(f"no recipes found in {lib}")
        sys.exit(1)
    sys.exit(run(paths, quiet=a.quiet))

> **First time on this machine?** Read `LOCAL.md` in this folder. If it does not exist, run the

   definition in the browser sim, judge it frame by frame, then export a Studio kit. Every texture and

## First run: build the textures and meshes (once per machine)

## The standard (a 100-move anime-style showcase, verified in Studio 2026-10-29)

The bar this skill was tuned to: 20 characters and 100 moves, built with this skill, recorded and
verified in Studio. Judge every new effect against that level, never below it.

**What made it that standard. Do all of these:**
1. **Every element is the real thing** (RULE ZERO below). Weapons, creatures and a coffin are meshes, and
   a slam leaves a real crater with debris.
2. **Ultimates get the anime set-piece layer:** impact frames, an FOV punch, focus lines, letterbox and
   camera cuts (sim actions `fov`, `overlay`, `bloom`, below).
3. **Run the polish pass on every effect, last:** `sim/effects/fxpolish.py`, `polish(d)`.
   - An energy dome becomes a ForceField shell in the most saturated colour, around a Neon core at 0.6x
     size that goes out first.
   - Crater rims take the arena's stone colour.
   - Aura flames and sparks go on the Part, not an Attachment.
   - Coloured afterimages are at least 0.6 transparent.
   - Lingering smoke is smaller and see-through.
4. **Saturated colour, never a pale mix.** A pale dome draws as clear glass, and a pale core blooms to
   white. For a darkness move, make the world pale and let the darkness be the black, with no additive
   glow on the black.
5. **The target reacts like a body** (next section). A hit on a body that floats upright reads as
   broken, however good the particles are.
6. **The camera frames the whole action.** Check the first and last frame of every cut, keep end
   close-ups at 4-5 studs, and never put the lens inside the caster.

**The gate before a recording.** Every check must pass, judged on numbers, not by eye:

| Check | Pass |
|---|---|
| `python sim/tools/sa_parent_check.py` | 0 SurfaceAppearances off a MeshPart |
| `lune run sim/tools/lune/build_check.luau <kits/*.luau>` (run from a folder whose `aftman.toml` or `rokit.toml` lists Lune) | every kit OK |
| `lune run sim/tools/lune/compile_check.luau <scripts>` | every script OK |
| `node sim/tools/phys_audit.js [prefix]` | no gap, sink, hover or STILL DOWN line |
| A sim snap of every move at its beats (`sim/snap.js`), tiled into one sheet per character | looked at once |
| One full warm play of every move in Studio before the real take | without it, fresh MeshPart + SurfaceAppearance pairs show "being generated" |
| The take itself | 0 "being generated" warnings; 0 effect or caster touches on the target; the get-up's lowest point at least -0.05; worst frame about 40 ms |

## A target that reacts like a body (measured in Studio)

The proven module is `references/HitSystem.luau`. It drives a knock with a thrown, tumbling R6 body,
and every rule below fixed a defect seen in Studio:
- **Going limp takes three steps:** `PlatformStand = true`, then `ChangeState(Enum.HumanoidStateType.Physics)`,
  then `EvaluateStateMachine = false`. Disabling the state machine alone leaves the Humanoid balancing the
  body. That was the "pushed, then stands upright in the air" bug.
- **A lift VectorForce must include the HumanoidRootPart.** It is 2.8 of an R6's 12.6 mass, so without it
  every throw falls short.
- **Use collision groups.** Every effect part goes in an FX group: the kit folder, its `_Actors` model
  (hooked with DescendantAdded and workspace.ChildAdded) and the caster. The target goes in a target
  group, and the two groups do not collide. Kit debris was sapping the launch speed, and the caster's
  limbs were bumping the body.
- **A body resting upright is toppled.** It counts as resting below 2 studs/s for 0.25 s, or when upright
  (UpVector.Y > 0.35) below 5 studs/s for 0.4 s. An upright body gets a push plus an AngularVelocity at
  6 rad/s for 0.4 s, with a fallback get-up 1.2 s later.
- **The get-up is planted on the floor.** Raycast the floor (the arena first, then the terrain). Build
  the body's boxes from RootJoint and every Motor6D (C0 * C1:Inverse(), half Part1.Size). On every frame
  of the 0.5 s Quad Out rise, put the root where the lowest corner sits on the floor. Place the first
  frame at once, so there is no one-frame pop.
- **A stagger slide never takes the root below floor + 3.**
- **A ragdoll must be the last hit:** a later flinch re-anchors the body.
- **Between moves:** the director calls `HitSystem.recover(target)` and waits for `isStanding` (2 s cap),
  so the body gets up on screen, then holds max(0.3, 0.8 - elapsed) s before the next move.
- **The sim models the same body:** `w.foe` with modes stand, fly, down and getup. `phys_audit.js`
  checks it.

## Measured in Roblox Studio (2026-10-27): the sim is calibrated to these

The sim was compared against real Studio frames for three hard effects (a water-dragon spell, a
phoenix dive, Crimson Detonation) and fixed until it predicted Studio. Trust these over any earlier note:

- **ParticleEmitter Size = HALF the drawn width** (Size 4 draws 8 studs). The sim
  draws 2 x Size; builders author the width they want to SEE and
  `effects/roblox_units.py` halves Size on write (`sizeConvention: "roblox"`). A
  builder that writes JSON itself must call `to_roblox_units()`.
- **SurfaceAppearance emissive saturates and never blooms**: white-hot comes from
  Neon or LightEmission particles, never from mesh emissive. Emission colour is
  surface colour x EmissiveTint. Unlit surfaces go much darker at night, so give
  night smoke more emissive.
- **PointLights light surfaces in Roblox, not in the sim**: fade them out, or they
  paint bands on nearby meshes.
- **No solid-core texture on a huge plane** (it becomes a solid disc): `glow_falloff`.
- **Preload every template at join**, not right before play.
- **Mesh upload route: OBJ -> FBX turns meshes 180 deg about Y.** Open Cloud rejects
  .obj, and the obvious Blender conversion (import -Z forward / Y up, export -Z / Y)
  lands OBJ -Z on Roblox +Z, so every mesh came in backwards (the phoenix flew
  tail-first; the dragon led horns-first). Use `sim/mesh/obj_to_fbx.py`, which adds a
  half turn before export. Symmetric meshes hide this, so check orientation with an
  asymmetric one (red block at -Z, blue at +Z).
- **To verify a change in Studio**, export the same JSON as a kit (`sim/studio_kit.js`), capture Studio
  at the same times, and lay the frames side by side: old sim | sim | Studio.

## Learned building 100 anime-style moves (2026-10-27 to 10-29)

Silent failures: each looked fine in one place and broke in another.
- **A CFrame tween turns the SHORT way round** (sim slerp = TweenService), so a
  260 deg spin turns -100 deg and a 720 deg spin does not turn at all. Spin with
  `{"do":"spin", target, axis:"X|Y|Z", rate:deg/s, time}`; it layers over a tween
  or path on the same part. `fxmore.circle()` uses it now.
- **Preload SurfaceAppearance maps BY ID.** `PreloadAsync` on the instance did not
  fetch the ColorMap: a crater plane drew as a solid tinted square until the map
  streamed in. The kit's `M.preload` now asks for every map and MeshId string too.
- **A fresh upload can say "Asset content representation is being generated" for
  30+ min, and Studio keeps that failure for the session.** Generation seems to
  start on the first request. Save, restart the window, run again.
- **Additive white stacks to a blown-out disc on a BIG orb** (a 5-stud spinning orb, a
  16-stud spirit orb). Size the core glow down, colour the swirls (no white start),
  and use a non-Neon body under a spinning textured shell.
- **A thin textured crescent band vanishes;** a wave wants a real crescent-moon mesh
  in Neon (`crescent_wall` in `sim/mesh/make_meshes.py`).
- **Frame strips must preload meshes**: a mesh was fetched only when its part first
  showed, asynchronously, so a synchronous strip never drew a NEW mesh. `index.html`
  now fetches every MeshId on load. `app.ready()` returns a Promise: await it.
- **Fit the camera to the WHOLE action**: half the sim fixes were framing (caster
  cropped at the edge, a blade poking into the lens, a camera inside a domain
  sphere). Check the first and last frame of every camera cut.
- **Luau allows 200 locals per function**: a kit with ~200 instances (a part-built shrine, a giant
  spirit armour) failed to compile. `studio_kit.js` now keeps template instances in a table (`I[n]`).
- **An emitter under an Attachment ignores its Shape**: a Box aura or an Inward sphere of motes all
  spawn at ONE point (an aura's flames were born inside the caster's torso; a "storm" of cut sprites
  became starbursts). Shaped emitters go straight under the Part.
- **Impact frames** (anime white/black flash with silhouettes): Neon dome + floor + Highlights on caster and
  target. A Highlight on a mesh does NOT fill seen from inside it, and Highlights switch a frame before a
  part shows. A two-tone silhouette impact frame on an extreme close-up draws one giant blob: on a
  close-up use solid colour frames. Measured: impact frames in 4 of 4 ultimates and 0 of 9 ordinary moves.
- Sim/kit actions for the set-piece layer: `{"do":"fov", by, i, o}` (FOV punch), `{"do":"overlay", kind:"lines"|"bars"}`
  (ScreenGui focus lines / letterbox), `{"do":"bloom"}`; Highlight Adornee "Foe" = the target (h.target);
  shake + FOV go through one camera driver that removes last frame's offset (an earlier shake drifted).
- Anchored ropes (tendrils, whips) are NOT path+lag (that slides like a serpent): pin the root and
  animate the rope's points as their own paths.
- Two stacked greyscale CCs inverted chroma in the sim (saturation summed past -1); clamped now.
- **A camera CUT during a running camera tween is lost in Roblox** (the tween keeps writing CFrame until it
  ends; the sim cancelled it): kits now cancel the running camera tween on every camera event.
- Frame review: `sim/snap.js` (`eval(await (await fetch('snap.js')).text()); await snap(file, name, times)`).
- `{"do":"timescale"}` sets every emitter's TimeScale; 0 = time stop, live particles hang, and particles
  Emit()ted while frozen are born frozen, so a frozen FLARE hangs as a white blob: emit only sparks/bursts
  in stopped time, or `clear` the flare. Also `{"do":"target","hide"}`; actor `model` = another rig or
  `"@target"` (a copy of the real target, joints driven, real clothes); key `move` (Motor6D.Transform with
  a translation: limbs float off their joints), `scale` (Model:ScaleTo per frame, re-read C0/C1/Size
  after), `fade` (LocalTransparencyModifier).
- `Enum.EasingStyle["Constant"]` errors in Roblox: the kit's easeV treats Constant as a step key and falls
  back on unknown styles.
- Close-ups must allow for the rig's props: a hat or a 6.8-stud cloak fills a 3-stud close-up; keep end
  shots at 4-5 studs and look away from the sun. Sim-snap every opener: a 2-3 stud close-up at
  FORM/CHANT/POINT puts the lens inside the caster.
- Linger smoke from a slam at the target drifts over end close-ups: cut `linger` on non-ultimates.
- A DARK aura must not glow: an additive glow layer over black flames reads as red candy floss. Give a dark
  aura LightEmission 0, so the envelope is a non-additive black haze.
- A Neon core inside an energy dome must take the dome's most SATURATED colour. A pale mix blooms to white
  on every dome; `"noCore": True` drops it for a black dome or a self-lit body.
- The sim renders ForceField material as additive white glare whatever its colour. Judge ForceField domes
  in Studio only. In Studio a ForceField dome shows its colour only when the colour is SATURATED: a pale
  tint draws as clear glass with a white rim, dark crimson reads as a real shell. The polish pass gives the
  shell the most saturated colour.
- A Ball part's inside is culled. For a sky you stand inside, use a mesh sphere in Neon: self-lit, so the
  inside faces read even though their normals point away.
- A world gone dark makes a darkness move unreadable. Make the WORLD pale and colourless and let the
  darkness be the black.
- A split-the-sky shot needs a DENSE cloud deck (~100 puffs, 9-15 studs). Thirty scattered puffs read as
  nothing torn.
- A Neon mesh carrying a soft-glow SurfaceAppearance reads as a blob. A plain Neon mesh shows its silhouette.
- A `path` step rebuilds the part's rotation from its travel direction every frame and keeps only its
  `offset`: a tilt set on the starting CFrame is thrown away. Put the tilt in `offset` (a shuriken volley
  flew edge-on, a dark sliver, until it was).
- Streak particles on a SPINNING part come out as vertical "rain" sticks in Studio. Put the streak on a
  Trail on a separate carrier part that rides the same path without spinning.
- A creature summon in Neon with a big flame emitter on it reads as a yellow cloud. Plain Neon, a small
  emitter, and a REAL mesh of that creature (a dog mesh standing in for a fox read as a blob; a modelled
  fox with tall ears read at once).
- A SurfaceAppearance can only be parented to a MeshPart: on a plain Part Studio refuses the whole kit.
  Use a MeshPart (a cube mesh) for a textured slab. The Lune build_check catches it (it stubs
  CreateMeshPartAsync), and so does `sim/tools/sa_parent_check.py`.
- A SurfaceAppearance texture can draw untextured (pale) for ~1 s the first time its part shows, even after
  a warm play. Draw the part from t=0 somewhere hidden (under the floor) so the texture is in before its beat.

Character moves (caster animation) in the sim and `studio_kit.js`: `def.rig` keys
drive the real caster's Motor6Ds; `def.actors` = runtime clones of the caster (shadow
clones); key `stretch: {RightArm: k | [k, width]}` lengthens/thickens a limb with
the joint end held (exact in Lune); `{"do":"ghost", parts, keep}` = afterimages of
chosen parts; a Highlight with Adornee "Dummy" wraps the caster; `{"do":"face"}`
calls `h.setFace`; `{"do":"hit", damage, knock, reaction, stun, time, ultimate}` goes
to the game's hit system (knock = a deterministic displacement, so effects can be
placed where the target WILL be).

## Learned on a sim-only showcase (disasters on a toy town, MP4 rendered from the sim)

Worth knowing for any "show the effects without Studio" request.
- **`fxpolish.polish()` turns every fire-shell `lumpy_sphere` into a ForceField shell + Neon core, and the sim
  draws a big ForceField as a WHITE BLOB.** A black hole's shock shell and a meteor's fire dome both rendered as
  white ovals. For a sim-rendered video write two files: `<name>.studio.json` with the full polish (right for
  Studio) and `<name>.json` with every step except `domes()` (`smoke(ghosts(auras(craters(d))))`).
- **`TL.flash()` writes Brightness back to 0** on the grade it flashes. If the scene darkens with a grade tween
  (a storm), every flash undoes the darkness: give flashes their own `grade() | {"name": "Flash"}`.
- **A mesh's Size scales its bounding box**, so parts modelled in one shared space (a body, its jaw, its leg)
  stay aligned only if each is placed with `place(origin, centre * K)` and sized `box_of(mesh, K)`.
- **Ragdoll bodies in the sim:** three meshes per body (stand, panic, flail), swapped by Transparency. Fly the
  flail along a `path` with `spin` (deterministic, so the landing spot is known). On landing, lay it flat, emit
  dizzy stars, then swap back to the stand mesh at the landing point (a get-up).
- **Check every camera position against the scene's buildings** before stripping. Four of six first cuts had
  the lens inside a house or a roof filling the frame. A wide set (a 232-stud wave) needs the side camera
  outside its width.
- **A ground plane at y=0.03 z-fights the sim's own floor** at distance (the grass blinked in chunks). Put it at
  y=0.2 and decals at 0.3+.
- **Video:** `app.captureFrame(t, 1920, 1080, q)` POSTed to `/save` runs about 3 frames/s with the tab fronted,
  much slower in a background tab. Start the loop un-awaited in the page (progress in a window variable), wait
  on the frame count from a background shell loop, then `ffmpeg -framerate 60 -i <name>_%05d.jpg` per effect
  plus title cards, concatenated with `-c copy`. A long render can crash the tab (it did at frame 5,343 of
  5,808), so wait on a loop that flags a stall, and resume from the last frame. Retry each frame's POST: a single
  failed fetch killed the first render. Run ffmpeg from Python with `-nostdin`, `stdin=DEVNULL` and
  `capture_output=True`: with inherited handles in a background shell it crashed.
- **A small creature mesh does not scale to a giant boss.** Its 1024 texture bake went scabby and blurry at 30x.
  Build a jointed block version of the design instead, posed by forward kinematics with CFrame tweens, so
  joints can't fight a `swing`.

## Learned putting 20 disaster effects in a real game (2026-11-02)

Sim sheets first, then a real-game capture of every effect. What only the game showed:
- **Build for the camera the game really starts on.** The effects were judged at zoom 165 and the game opens at 90: a dragon at 58 studs flew above the frame. Either keep tall things inside the frustum or ease the camera out for the effect, then give the view back.
- **A kit source past 200,000 characters will not install.** Stepped keyframes and many one-use carriers get there fast: reuse one carrier for every same-look part instead of one per use.
- **Cel smoke at the sim's default colour reads as black blobs from above.** Keep it above about 0.45 grey, at 0.3 transparency, with low LightInfluence, and cut rates hard. Smoke over a pit or a beam hides the effect.
- **Emissive on a textured sheet blows out to a pale wash.** A lava sheet wants 0.5-0.8, with thin cracks: a noise band picks far more of the map than it looks like it should.
- **Judge the real game with Studio focused and not minimised.** Unfocused it drops to a crawl and stills repeat; minimised, screen capture fails. Hide tutorial cards during a capture, and aim drops at the middle of town, not at the crowd.

## RULE ZERO: no shortcuts, ever

**Every effect is built to the best result possible. If an effect needs a
thing, make the thing.** A spell that is a creature gets a real creature mesh;
a weapon gets a real weapon; a book gets a real book; a new look gets its own
texture. Never substitute an existing generic piece (a beam, a blob, a box, a
reused texture) because it is quicker. Shortcuts are exactly what make effects
boring. This overrides time and token budget.

The failure that set this rule: a water-dragon spell shipped as a layered water
beam with a lumpy sphere for a head, when the spell is an eastern water dragon.
It needed a Blender dragon head, a serpentine segmented body that follows the
head's path, water textures for both, and was rebuilt that way (`sim/mesh/make_dragon.py`).

The audit that followed found the same stand-in in 29 effects, so check these first: craters painted as decals and rocks as flat sprites (use `crater()` + `debris()`), props as boxes (books, swords), a named weapon style with no weapons (a three-sword style needs three swords), a lance that is only a beam, a flower spell with petals but no flowers, a punch barrage whose fists are glow sprites. Sprites are fine as a LAYER (gravel, dust, sparks) on top of the real object, never instead of it.

Before calling any effect done, ask of every visible element: **"is this what
the effect actually IS, or a stand-in for it?"** List each stand-in and replace
it (Blender mesh, programmatic texture, new helper, new sim feature) before
rendering. If the sim cannot show what the effect needs, extend the sim.

A VFX effect is not an asset. It is about thirty numbers per layer plus a texture
reference. That single fact decides this skill's whole architecture: effects are
**definitions you own**, and with the generated textures and meshes, so is everything they draw.

## The sim: build and judge effects outside Studio

`sim/` is a browser simulator of Roblox's VFX instances with Roblox's own
property names and value types: ParticleEmitter (every property, flipbooks,
all four orientations, shapes, drag, squash, ZOffset, LightEmission blend),
Beam (Bezier from attachment +X/-X, segments, texture modes, scroll), Trail,
Part/MeshPart (Neon, ForceField, TextureID), PointLight/SpotLight, Highlight,
ColorCorrectionEffect, BloomEffect, plus a timeline (emit / set / tween with
Roblox easing / enable / shake). Deterministic: seek(t) replays at 1/60 s, so
frame N always looks the same.

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `sim/vfxsim.js` | simulation core, no DOM (runs under node), plus `toLuau()` exporter and `fromRecipe()` importer |
| `sim/vfxrender.js` | three.js r128 renderer, bloom + colour-correction post, `metrics()` (luma / sat / >250 fraction) |
| `sim/index.html` | the workbench page (inspector, timeline, JSON, Luau tabs); lists `sim/effects/index.json` |
| `sim/effects/*.json` | effect definitions (recipe codec values, CFrame = [x,y,z,rxDeg,ryDeg,rzDeg]); yours go here too |
| `sim/effects/build_*.py` | parametric builders, one per effect; three worked examples ship |
| `sim/tex/make_textures.py` | the base textures, generated from maths (white + alpha so Color tints them) |
| `sim/mesh/make_meshes.py` | Blender VFX meshes (U along motion, V across), OBJ shared by sim and Roblox upload |
| `sim/serve.py` | local server; `POST /save?name=x.png` writes a strip to `sim/out/` |

**Cheap check loop:** `python sim/serve.py`, open it in a browser Claude can drive,
then one JavaScript call: `await app.ready(); const s = await
app.strip([3,4,6,8,12].map(f=>f/60)); await fetch('/save?name=s.png',
{method:'POST', body:s.png})` and read ONE strip image plus `s.metrics`.
Judge timing on numbers first (flash frames, luma peak), the image once.

**Behaviour marked CALIBRATE in the code is inferred, not measured:** Drag
(halvings per second), Squash exponent, Disc ShapePartial meaning, flipbook
frame order, beam texture v side, VelocityPerpendicular in-plane axes, bloom
threshold scale. Calibrate each against Studio once (same JSON through
`toLuau`, phase-frozen capture, compare) before trusting fine detail.
